This is an fMRI, task-based, within-subject study contrasting deceptive versus honest responses (deceptive > honest), which operationalizes interference-monitoring/resolution and inhibitory control—an executive function domain. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster results and coordinate tables, and provides participant demographics (mean age 23), healthy sample status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and detailed task paradigm. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and thus appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of planning (Tower of London) in healthy adult participants (ages 19–39). The paper reports within-participant contrasts manipulating planning parameters (search depth and goal hierarchy) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected results reported; coordinate tables and figures provided). Participant characteristics, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly described. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met. No exclusion criteria apply: the study is not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, includes within-group healthy participant contrasts, and participants are within the 18–60 range. Full text is complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, References).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cognitive control using a cued Stroop paradigm in healthy adults (ages 20–38). It reports within-subject modeling of congruent and incongruent trials (and sensory-conflict–weighted regressors), group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps within the prefrontal mask with peak coordinates and thresholds, and psychophysiological interaction analyses. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and task details are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; includes whole-brain maps; not connectivity-only; healthy within-age-range sample). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=10, ages 19–35) explicitly investigating inhibitory/executive processes during preparation. It includes within-subject contrasts of an executive-control task versus an active control (Preparation > Watch), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5) with FDR correction and coordinate/figure reporting. Task paradigm maps onto inhibition/executive control and working/preparatory control domains. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task details are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Thus all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion (E3): The study used PET to measure serotonin transporter (SERT) binding at rest and correlated these molecular PET measures with separately administered cognitive tests. It did not perform task-based PET/fMRI activation paradigms during executive function tasks, did not report within-participant task vs active-control contrasts, and did not present group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps — analyses are ROI-based correlations rather than task-evoked activation maps. Inclusion criteria met: I9 (executive-function tasks such as Stroop and TMT B were used) and I10 (participant age, healthy status, imaging modality (PET), and task paradigms are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no task-based PET/fMRI assessing executive function during imaging), I6 (no within-participant contrast of task vs active control during imaging), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map), I8 (no qualifying whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is a task-based, event-related fMRI study of set-shifting (cognitive flexibility) in healthy young adults using the Wisconsin Word Sorting Task. The paper reports within-participant contrasts against an active control condition (control matching), performs group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with thresholding and reports peak coordinates/tables and figures, and provides participant demographics and imaging/task details. The task clearly falls within executive function (cognitive flexibility/set-shifting). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, includes active control baseline, empirical, healthy adults within 18–60). Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion, tables, references) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 18–55) using the Attention Network Test. It includes an explicitly reported within-subject executive-control contrast (incongruent > congruent), and reports group-level second-level voxelwise results with coordinates (within-sample task effects and genotype group comparisons). Participant demographics, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are all described. Although ROI masks were defined for hypothesis testing, the manuscript reports voxelwise activation coordinates from the within-group (whole-sample) task analysis, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, group-level task-evoked results. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only results, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, resting baseline only, non-empirical, or out-of-range participants) are met. Full text appears complete with background, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of executive control (go/nogo/voluntary selection) in adults that reports within-subject contrasts (selection+/- and selection vs go/nogo and control conditions). Group-level, whole-brain analyses are reported for healthy controls (tables/figures/coordinates are presented), and ROI analyses are supplementary; the paper provides participant ages and confirmation of healthy control status, imaging modality (1.5 T fMRI), and full task details. The task falls into established executive domains (inhibition/response selection/initiative). No exclusion criteria are met: whole-brain maps are reported (not ROI-only), results include within-group healthy participant contrasts (not only between-group), and an active control task was used. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion: E8 applies — the study includes a clinical ADHD group and is not restricted to healthy individuals, which violates the review’s requirement for healthy-only samples. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of an executive function—inhibition Go/No-Go), I6 (within-participant contrasts such as No-Go vs Go and slow vs fast), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps were reported), I8 (whole-brain results described in text/tables/figures), I9 (task falls within executive function domain: inhibition), I10 (participant ages, sample status for controls, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: [] (all relevant I5–I10 were satisfied). Full text completeness: fulltext_incomplete=false (full article text including methods, results, and discussion provided). Because the study includes non-healthy participants (ADHD patients), it must be excluded per E8 despite meeting the inclusion criteria and reporting usable within-group healthy-control contrasts.

This PET study (15O H2O) reports task-based, within-participant voxelwise contrasts of ambivalent (cognitive conflict) vs univalent conditions, with SPM whole-brain group analyses and tables/figures of coordinates. The task probes evaluative conflict resolution and search-related working memory (executive/cognitive control processes). Healthy control within-group contrasts are reported, participant demographics and imaging modality are provided, and contrasts use an active control (univalent conditions). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study uses task-based fMRI of an executive function (go/no-go inhibition) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates, but it should be excluded for two reasons: (1) Exclusion E8: the sample is not restricted to healthy adults (study includes Parkinson’s disease patients and controls), so it does not meet the requirement for studies of healthy-only participants. (2) Exclusion E6: the primary within-subject contrast reported is activation versus rest (A>R) using a passive baseline rather than an active control condition, and the inclusion criterion I6 requires a within-participant contrast against an active control. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: I6. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study using an n-back working memory task (executive function) in healthy adult participants (mean age 23.3). Analyses include within-subject contrasts (e.g., Clever vs Stupid primes; error vs correct trials) and group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistical mapping (conjunction analyses corrected for multiple comparisons and exploratory whole-brain searches; coordinates and SPM results reported). Task paradigm, imaging modality, participant demographics, and methods are fully described. The study therefore meets all required inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function fMRI with whole-brain group results and reports coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; within healthy 18–60 sample; active control conditions used). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this study uses task-based fMRI of an executive/inhibition task (Stroop) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results, it is a patient vs control study that reports primarily between-group contrasts (patients>controls) without presenting an accompanying within-group task activation map for the healthy control group. Thus it violates exclusion E5. In addition, the sample is not restricted to healthy adults (includes patients with essential tremor), meeting exclusion E8. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI executive task), I6 (within-participant cognitive>baseline contrast generated), I7 (group-level whole-brain analyses reported), I8 (coordinates/figures reported), I9 (task within executive/inhibition domain), I10 (sample status, imaging modality, and paradigm described). Inclusion criteria not met: none. Because E5 (only between-group contrasts without within-group healthy activation maps) and E8 (not restricted to healthy individuals) are met, the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis of executive function activations in healthy adults.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults (mean age 23) using a task (PPA) that manipulates relational integration and interference resolution—both executive/cognitive-control processes. Analyses include within-participant contrasts across task conditions (RC and IN factorial contrasts) and report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (whole-brain maps/tables/figures), with ROI and small-volume corrections described. Participant health status, ages, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are violated.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study of executive function (cognitive set shifting) with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and adequate reporting of participants, modality, and paradigm, the paper uses fixation/rest as the baseline for within-participant contrasts and does not employ an active control condition. This violates inclusion criterion I6 and meets exclusion criterion E6 (rest/fixation as the only baseline). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criterion not met: I6. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults (age 18–55) using a semantic verbal fluency task (executive function initiation/working memory aspects) with an active high-level baseline (reading aloud). The paper reports within-subject contrasts (semantic verbal fluency > reading aloud) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM results with peak coordinates and cluster extent). Participant characteristics, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group only, healthy adult sample within age range).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (Stroop inhibition/selective attention) in healthy adults (ages 22–40). It reports within-subject contrasts (incongruent minus congruent) serving as active control comparisons, conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses with thresholding and presents results in figures and tables of Talairach coordinates (including conjunction analyses). Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigms are clearly described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not resting-state baseline only, empirical human neuroimaging data, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (SST variant) in healthy adults that reports within-subject contrasts and group-level whole-brain analyses (FWE-corrected). However, the full text does not report participant ages nor an explicit statement confirming the sample as healthy (methods list 'Fourteen right handed participants' but no ages or explicit health status). Inclusion criterion I10 requires reporting of participant age and confirmation of healthy sample status; this information is missing, so not all inclusion criteria are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered: whole-brain results are reported and this is not a connectivity-only, between-group, rest-baseline-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range-age study based on available text. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded because I10 is not satisfied.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of executive function (inhibition, attentional shifting, response initiation). It includes within-participant contrasts (e.g., stop–go, shift–go, stop–shift, double–stop) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with corrected statistics and peak coordinates. Participant information (healthy adults aged 18–40), imaging modality (3T fMRI), and detailed task paradigms are provided. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This PET study used an auditory continuous performance task (vigilance) in healthy adults and reports group-level, whole-brain SPM results and coordinate tables. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (PET task-based study), I7 (group whole-brain voxelwise maps), I8 (coordinates/figures reported), I9 (task falls within executive domain: vigilance/attention), I10 (participant age and healthy sample and imaging modality reported). However, the PET analyses use a block-design Task versus Rest contrast (rest baseline only) and do not include a within-participant contrast of the executive task versus an active control condition. Therefore I6 is not satisfied, and exclusion criterion E6 (rest/fixation as the only baseline without an active control) is met. Although ERP data separate target vs non-target, the qualifying whole-brain PET maps are Task vs Rest only, so the study does not meet the required within-task active-control contrast.

This study used PET [11C]raclopride to measure striatal dopamine binding and administered executive-function tasks (delayed-response working memory, Tower of London planning) behaviorally. However, no task-evoked, within-participant neuroimaging contrasts or group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) activation maps are reported. Imaging results are limited to striatal binding (ROI) and correlations with behavioral change rather than task-based activation mapping. Therefore it does not meet the meta-analysis requirements for within-subject task contrasts or whole-brain task activation reporting.

This study used FDG-PET acquired during a rest/passive introspection condition (no task performed in scanner) and related resting metabolism to CPT performance measured separately. Therefore it does not provide a task-based within-participant contrast (no task vs active control), nor does it report group-level whole-brain task activation maps. Analyses were region-focused (predefined prefrontal ROIs) rather than whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results, and the sample included bipolar patients (not restricted to healthy adults). Inclusion criteria met: I9 (CPT/vigilance is an executive attention task) and I10 (participant characteristics, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (task-based fMRI/PET with task in scanner), I6 (within-participant task vs active control contrast), I7 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map), I8 (no whole-brain results reported). Exclusion criteria met: E3 (ROI-only analyses/no whole-brain results), E6 (resting scan without an active control task), E8 (study includes patient group; not restricted to healthy individuals). Full text appears complete.

This PET study of an auditory continuous performance task (CPT) meets several inclusion criteria: I5 (PET study of executive/attention task), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM maps reported), I8 (coordinates/tables and figures reported), I9 (task = vigilance/attention within executive domains), and I10 (participant ages, healthy status, PET modality, and task paradigm reported). However, it fails I6: there is no within-participant contrast of the executive task against an active control condition—the PET analyses use Task versus Rest (passive baseline). This violates exclusion criterion E6 (studies using rest/fixation as the only baseline). Note: while ERP data include target vs non-target contrasts, the imaging (PET) whole-brain maps used for meta-analysis are Task vs Rest. Therefore the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

This study is excluded because it is not a task-based executive-function activation study and violates several exclusion criteria. Exclusion IDs met: E3, E4, E5, E6, E8. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (no task-based fMRI/PET of executive function; PET data are resting FDG scans after drug/placebo), I6 (no within-participant contrast of an executive task vs active control), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported; analyses are ROI-based), I9 (imaging was not acquired during an executive task paradigm despite behavioral working memory testing), I10 (participants are not a healthy sample restricted to age 18–60; sample is male veterans aged 52–81 including PTSD patients). The full text appears complete and provides methods/results/discussion, but the imaging design and sample do not meet the meta-analysis inclusion requirements.

Exclusion justified because the study includes participants older than 60 years (E8) and uses a rest baseline (eyes-open rest) as the comparison condition rather than an active control task (E6). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (PET study of an executive function task — working memory), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported via SPM and coordinate tables/figures), I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables and described in text), I9 (task is working memory, an established executive domain), and I10 (participant age, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criterion I6 is not met because the primary within-participant contrasts are task versus rest rather than task versus an active control condition. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Given the violations of E6 and E8, the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis despite satisfying other inclusion criteria.

Full text is complete. Excluded because the study includes participants outside the target healthy adult range and is not restricted to healthy individuals (E8). Although the study uses PET and a within-participant contrast versus an active control and reports whole-brain voxelwise results, the task (visual navigation) is not within the specified executive function domains required by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (within-participant contrast vs active control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described), I10 (participant information, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (study does not assess a canonical executive function/cognitive control task), I9 (task does not fall within listed executive function domains such as working memory, inhibition, flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore excluded based on E8.

Exclusion criteria met: E3 (study conducted ROI-masked analyses focused on prefrontal ROIs without reporting group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps) and E8 (participants are elderly and include MCI patients — sample not restricted to healthy adults aged 18–60). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (PET study of executive function/dual-tasking), I6 (within-participant contrasts comparing dual vs. single task active control conditions), I8 (results clearly described in text/figures/tables), I9 (task falls within executive function domain), I10 (participant ages/health status, imaging modality, and paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no reported group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis restricted to healthy adults aged 18–60 and requiring whole-brain task activation maps.

Exclusion summary: This study is excluded because it reports only between-group comparisons of resting 18F-FDG PET metabolism in methamphetamine users vs controls and does not provide any task-evoked, within-participant activation contrasts in healthy adults. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (only between-group contrasts without within-group task activation in healthy participants), E6 (imaging consists of rest/eyes-closed baseline without an active in-scanner task), E8 (sample is not restricted to healthy participants — includes clinical MA users). Inclusion criteria met: none of the required imaging-task criteria are satisfied. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no task-based fMRI/PET assessing executive function — PET was resting metabolism), I6 (no within-participant task vs active control contrast), I7 (no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map — whole-brain maps are for resting group differences), I8 (coordinate-reporting criterion is irrelevant because there is no task-evoked map), I9 (no in-scanner executive task; WCST was performed outside the scanner), I10 (imaging task paradigm for executive task not reported as an in-scanner task). Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion. Thus the study does not meet the meta-analysis inclusion criteria.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is a PET study of an executive function paradigm (spatial working memory) (I5); it reports within-participant contrasts of the executive task versus an active visuomotor control (SWT vs VMT) (I6); it provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical mapping using SPM (I7) with coordinate/table and figure reporting (I8); the task falls within the executive domain (working memory) (I9); and participant demographics, healthy control status, imaging modality, and task details are reported (I10). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and is complete. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore I include the study.

This article is a quantitative meta-analysis aggregating coordinates from published fMRI studies rather than reporting original task-evoked neuroimaging data from participants. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E7 (non-empirical paper / meta-analysis without original human neuroimaging data). The study does address executive-function tasks (task-switching and Stroop) and reports coordinates and sample/modality details (meeting I9 and I10, and I8 insofar as results are reported in tables), but it does not itself present original fMRI/PET within-participant task contrasts or group-level whole-brain statistical maps (inclusion criteria I5, I6, and I7 are not met). Full text appears complete. Given E7 is met, the study must be excluded.

The study is a PET task-based investigation with within-participant baseline vs gambling contrasts, but it does not provide group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-activation maps and focuses analyses on the ventral striatum (ROI-targeted). Exclusion criteria met: E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) and E8 (study includes pathological gamblers — not restricted to healthy individuals). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (within-participant contrast of task vs active control) and I10 (participant age, healthy sample info for controls, imaging modality PET, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (unclear/does not target an established executive function domain listed), I7 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise activation map), I8 (no whole-brain results in acceptable formats), and I9 (task—IGT—does not clearly fall within the specified executive function domains). Full text appears complete: fulltext_incomplete=false.

Although the study includes executive function tasks (working memory, learning) and reports behavioral effects, it does not present within-participant task vs active-control PET/fMRI contrasts or group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps. Inclusion criteria met: I9 (tasks are within executive function domains) and I10 (participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality [PET], and task paradigms are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (does not functionally image task-evoked executive function activations using task-based PET/fMRI), I6 (no within-participant task vs active control neuroimaging contrast), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map), I8 (no qualifying whole-brain results reported). Full text appears complete for screening.

Although the study administered executive function tasks and reports participant demographics and PET modality, it does not provide task-evoked, within-participant whole-brain activation contrasts. PET data were resting FDG measures acquired prior to behavioral testing and correlations with behavior; no task-based PET/fMRI activation maps or within-subject task vs active-control contrasts are reported. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI/PET assessing executive function), I6 (within-participant task vs active control contrast), I7 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps), and I8 (clear whole-brain task results). Exclusion criteria triggered: E4 (resting-state/task-less imaging without task activation maps) and E8 (study sample not restricted to healthy individuals; includes remitted MDD subjects). Conclusion: Exclude.

Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria I5 and I9. Although it reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (I7), provides results in figures/tables (I8), and reports participant, health, age, and imaging details (I10), it lacks any within-participant contrast of an executive function task (I6/I5). No exclusion criteria from the list are directly met. Hence the study is excluded for failing to assess an executive-function task domain required by the meta-analysis.
