Although this PET study reports whole-brain, group-level task contrasts (timing tasks versus an active control) with coordinates and sufficient participant/task information, the experimental paradigm probes motor/temporal timing (synchronization and continuation tapping) rather than established executive function domains. Moreover, the study includes Parkinson’s disease patients (not restricted to healthy individuals), which violates exclusion criterion E8. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (study does not assess executive function/cognitive control task), I9 (task not within established executive function domains). Therefore exclude.

Excluded because the study does not meet inclusion criterion I7 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analysis): although it reports group-level voxelwise contrasts, the imaging covered limited transverse slices (not whole-brain coverage), and the authors explicitly state they could not scan the whole brain. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI executive-function tasks: go/no-go and WCST), I6 (within-participant contrasts: no-go vs go), I8 (results reported in figures and coordinates), I9 (tasks are established executive domains: inhibition and set-shifting), and I10 (participant age, healthy sample, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). No exclusion criteria were violated (exclusion criteria applied: []). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Full text is complete. The study is an fMRI task-based, within-subject investigation of executive functions (WCST and n-back) and reports voxelwise activation with coordinates; it meets I5, I6, I8, I9 and I10. However, it does NOT meet I7: results are based on partial-brain coverage (four contiguous slices) rather than a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical map, so a qualifying whole-brain analysis is absent. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to satisfy inclusion criterion I7 (whole-brain evidence).

The study is an empirical, task-based fMRI investigation of response inhibition using a go–nogo paradigm in healthy adults and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses. It therefore satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI of executive control), I6 (within-participant contrasts such as NOGO vs GO), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (coordinates and whole-brain results described), and I9 (inhibition domain). However, I10 is not fully satisfied because the full text does not report participant ages or an age range (it only states “eighteen healthy subjects”), whereas I10 requires reporting of participant age information in addition to sample health status, imaging modality, and task. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because not all inclusion criteria are met (specifically I10).

This is a task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (go/no-go), an established executive function domain. It reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., no-go vs infrequent-go; infrequent-go vs frequent-go), group-level random-effects whole-brain voxelwise analyses with voxelwise thresholds and FDR correction, and provides tables/figures of activations. Participants are healthy adults (n=25; ages 20–27), right-handed, with imaging modality and task adequately described. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI Go/No-Go study of voluntary swallowing in healthy adults. Although it uses a Go/No-Go design, the study’s primary focus is sensorimotor control of swallowing rather than investigation of executive functions/cognitive control. Critically, the group-level analyses are ROI-based (counts of activated voxels within anatomically-defined ROIs with pairwise t-tests) rather than whole-brain, voxelwise group statistical maps. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). The study does report participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm (I10 met). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (study does not primarily assess executive function/cognitive control), I6 (no clear within-participant contrast of an executive-function task vs an active control in the sense required), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task map), I9 (task does not clearly fall within established executive function domains as framed by this meta-analysis). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Exclusion criteria met: E6 (the primary within-subject contrast reported and analyzed is Go/No-go > rest; rest/fixation is the only baseline used rather than an active control). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of an executive function — Go/No-go/inhibition), I7 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and within-group activation maps reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures), I9 (task falls within established executive function domain — inhibition), I10 (participant/sample, modality, and task details reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast of the executive function task relative to an active control condition). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Because I6 is not satisfied and E6 is met, this study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study reports a task-based fMRI investigation of sustained attention (vigilance, an executive function domain) including a healthy adult control group (ages 18–50). It contains within-participant contrasts against an active control (visual countdown baseline) and event-related contrasts (correct rejections vs. other trial types). The paper describes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (composite within-group activation maps with voxelwise one-sample t-tests and cluster correction), and reports whole-brain results in text/figures and ROI analyses. Participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are all reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria are met. Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is a single-subject fMRI case study (n=1) that reports within-subject planning > non-planning whole-brain voxelwise maps. However inclusion criterion I7 requires a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map. Although the study provides whole-brain maps and meets other inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I8, I9, I10), it does not provide group-level analyses and therefore does not satisfy I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of cognitive control (task switching) in healthy adults. It uses within-subject contrasts (mixed-task vs single-task; task-switch vs task-repeat) that probe executive function, and employs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects ANOVAs) with voxelwise and cluster-level thresholds. Participant demographics (N=13, age range 19–26, healthy), imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are reported in detail. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, uses active task contrasts beyond fixation, empirical human neuroimaging data, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and should be INCLUDED.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (age 23–35) using a go/no-go inhibitory control paradigm, which is an established executive function (inhibition). The design includes within-subject contrasts (no-go vs go) and a crossover manipulation; group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed using permutation-based mapping and cluster-level inference, with results reported as coordinates and figures. Participant health status, ages, imaging modality, and task paradigm are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group task activation, uses an active control condition, empirical human neuroimaging data, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and none of the exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study examines working memory using an audiospatial n-back task (1-, 2-, 3-back) in healthy adults (ages 20–30). It uses within-subject contrasts of memory load (3-back vs 1-back; 2-back vs 1-back), employs voxelwise, group-level whole-brain statistical analyses (voxelwise t-tests, Talairach coordinates reported, figures/tables), and reports participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task details. Working memory is an established executive-function domain. All required inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (whole-brain results are reported; not ROI-only; not connectivity/resting-only; not between-group only; active control used; empirical study with healthy adults within 18–60). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=45, ages 18–45) using established executive function paradigms (Go/No-Go inhibition; Reward/No-Reward; Loss/No-Loss). It reports within-subject contrasts (No-Go>Go, Reward>No-Reward, Loss>No-Loss) and group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM2 analyses with voxelwise thresholds and cluster reports; results are presented in figures and tables (coordinates). Participant health screening, imaging modality, and task paradigms are clearly reported. Thus all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an event-related fMRI study of cognitive control (task-switching Stroop) in healthy adults (N=12, ages 18–30). It reports within-subject contrasts (instruction: color naming > word reading; response: incongruent > congruent), group-level voxelwise spatial F maps pooled across subjects, and reports coordinates for activations. Imaging modality, participant age/health, and task paradigm are clearly described. Results include whole-brain analyses (spatial F maps) and coordinate reporting. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, uses active task contrasts, empirical with original human data, participants are within 18–60 and healthy). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Exclusion E3 met: authors report analyses restricted to preselected regions of interest (motor cortex and preSMA) rather than a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of an executive function/inhibition go/no-go task), I6 (within-participant contrast of go vs no-go), I9 (inhibition is an established executive function domain), I10 (participant ages and healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise map), I8 (not applicable because no qualifying whole-brain results reported). Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it violates two exclusion criteria: E3 and E8. E3: The reported neuroimaging results in the provided full text focus on activity within a scene-selective ROI (left parahippocampal/lingual gyrus) and ROI-based comparisons; no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps or whole-brain coordinate results are described in the main text, so it appears to report only ROI analyses. E8: The participant sample includes older adults aged 60–77 years, which falls outside the review’s eligible age range of 18–60. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of working memory/executive function), I6 (within-participant contrasts: remember vs ignore vs passive), I9 (task within executive function domain: working memory/inhibition), and I10 (participant ages reported, healthy sample, imaging modality and task paradigm described). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no evidence of a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of inhibition tasks in healthy participants that meets multiple inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) but must be excluded because participants are children/adolescents (mean age ~14.7 years), violating the review’s age restriction (Exclusion E8). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function/inhibition), I6 (within-participant contrasts: incongruent vs congruent, on vs off), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps and thresholded Z-stat images), I8 (results reported in text/tables/figures), I9 (tasks in inhibition domain), I10 (participant age, healthy status, imaging modality, and paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none (all applicable inclusions are satisfied). Exclusion criteria met: E8 (participants outside 18–60 years). Therefore EXCLUDED on grounds of E8.

This is an fMRI study of executive control (stop-signal task) in healthy adults (ages 22–42). It reports within-subject contrasts (stop vs go; post-stop stop-success vs post-go stop-success), uses group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses in SPM with reported coordinates and thresholding, and provides participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task details. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not resting-baseline only, participants are healthy and within 18–60). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an fMRI study using an n-back working memory task in healthy adults (age 21–29) with within-subject contrasts (0-, 1-, 2-back) including a linear memory-load contrast and memory load × stimulus interactions. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses were performed using SPM99 and results (including MNI coordinates and thresholding information) are reported. The task (working memory) is an established executive-function domain. Participant health status, age range, imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and task paradigm are all reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, baseline includes an active 0-back control, empirical human neuroimaging data, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and none of the exclusion criteria.

The study meets multiple inclusion criteria for the task-based neuroimaging meta-analysis (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10): it is an fMRI study (I5) using n-back working-memory tasks (I9) with within-participant contrasts (Simple subtraction of active control; I6), reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps/tables/figures for control adults (I7,I8), and provides participant ages, imaging modality, and task details (I10). However, it violates exclusion criterion E8: the sample is not restricted to healthy adults — the study includes children (ages 7–12) and clinical participants with FASD in addition to controls, and thus includes participants outside the 18–60 healthy-adult target and is not restricted to healthy individuals. Because E8 is met, the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis restricted to healthy adults. Full text appears complete.

Exclusion criterion E8 met: the study includes participants outside the 18–60 age range (healthy controls aged 49–70, with some controls up to 70) and the overall sample is not restricted to healthy individuals (Parkinson's disease patients are also included). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (PET study of executive function — Tower of London planning), I6 (within-participant contrasts via parametric analyses across task difficulty and task-level comparisons), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses), I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates and figures), I9 (planning is an established executive function), I10 (participant ages, health status of controls, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none (all applicable I5–I10 were satisfied). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

Meets all inclusion criteria for executive-function meta-analysis: a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults including an executive inhibition paradigm (Go/No-go). Contains a within-participant contrast (No-go vs Go), group-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported with thresholding and tables/figures of activations, and provides participant age, health screening, imaging modality, and task details. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical, event-related fMRI study of executive control tasks (Go/No-go, oddball, response selection) in healthy adults (mean age 22.9, range 18–27). It reports within-participant contrasts and group-level voxelwise random-effects ANOVAs across the whole brain, with tables/figures and coordinate reporting for activation loci. Tasks map to established executive domains (inhibition, selection/monitoring), imaging modality is fMRI, and participant health/age information is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and should be included.

Full text is complete. Met: I7 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts reported for black>white faces), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures), I10 (participant age/health, imaging modality, and paradigm reported). Not met: I5 (the fMRI paradigm does not assess an executive function — it is a face perception/spatial-location task), I6 (no within-participant contrast of an executive-function task vs an active control condition; contrasts are race of face and baseline), I9 (tasks do not fall within established executive-function domains; the Stroop inhibition measure was behavioral and measured in a separate session, not as an fMRI task). Exclusion IDs met: none ([]) . Because several required inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I9) are not satisfied, the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an event-related fMRI study of the Stroop color-word task in healthy adults (ages 20–45). It assesses an executive function (inhibition/cognitive control) using a task-based paradigm and reports within-participant contrasts (infrequent incongruent vs congruent trials; also an inverse Stroop contrast). Group-level, whole-brain composite statistical maps (voxelwise analyses, thresholded maps and ROI coordinate reporting) are presented and compared across subjects. Participant demographics, healthy status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, uses an active control, empirical human imaging, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/summary provided). Based on available content: no clear evidence that the task is an established executive function paradigm (I9 not met); no clear within-participant contrast of an executive function task versus an active control is described (I6 not met); no explicit statement of group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps or coordinates is provided (I7 not met); participant age/healthy-sample details and full task paradigm details are not reported here (I10 not met). The provided text also does not unambiguously demonstrate that the study assessed executive function/cognitive control as defined by our inclusion criteria (I5 not met). Therefore cannot confirm any inclusion criteria are satisfied. No exclusion criteria from E3–E8 can be confidently applied based on the abstract alone (exclusion_criteria_applied = []). Recommend obtaining the full article to re-assess. Inclusion criteria met: []. Inclusion criteria not met: ["I5","I6","I7","I9","I10"]. Exclusion criteria met: [].

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (an established executive function domain) in healthy adults (ages 20–34, plus additional behavioral sample 18–29). The paper reports within-participant contrasts of WM versus an active control condition, uses group-level whole-brain (random-effects, voxelwise) analyses with cluster correction, and provides coordinates/figures describing activations. Participant characteristics, imaging modality, and task paradigm are all reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete for screening purposes. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=10, ages 18–31) investigating planning and set-shifting — an executive function (cognitive flexibility/planning). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and thresholded (reports of coordinate peaks and figures), with within-subject contrasts (e.g., retrieval with shift vs control; retrieval with shift vs retrieval without shift; continuous shift vs control). Imaging modality, participant demographics/health status, and detailed task paradigm are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, enabling assessment against inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of response inhibition (stop-signal task) in healthy adult participants (ages 22–42). It uses task-based executive function paradigms (inhibition) and reports within-subject contrasts (successful vs failed stop trials). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported (FDR-corrected maps, coordinates, and figures/tables). Participant demographics, health status (healthy), imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task methods are provided. No exclusion criteria are violated (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group task activation maps in healthy adults within age range). Full text content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a non-empirical commentary/review article summarizing fMRI/PET work (e.g., Furey et al.) rather than an original empirical human neuroimaging study. It does not present methods, participant data, task-based within-subject contrasts, or group-level whole-brain activation maps. Therefore it fails to meet the required inclusion criteria and meets exclusion criterion E7 (non-empirical paper without original human neuroimaging data). Full text appears complete (commentary content present).

This fMRI study uses a task-based stop-signal paradigm probing response inhibition (an executive function). It reports within-participant contrasts (StopInhibit vs Go) and other Go/Stop contrasts, with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (thresholded and cluster-corrected) and reported activation coordinates. Participant demographic information (healthy, age 18–39), imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly described. The task falls within the inhibition domain of executive function. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., it is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts in healthy adults aged 18–60, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study uses task-based fMRI with a Stroop inhibitory-control paradigm and reports within-subject contrasts and voxelwise group maps in healthy comparison subjects, satisfying inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, the sample is not restricted to healthy adults (includes pathological gamblers) and the reported age range spans 18–65 years (exceeding the 18–60 range). Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E8 (participants outside 18–60 or not restricted to healthy individuals). Although within-group healthy activation maps are reported, E8 requires restriction to healthy adults and/or age within 18–60, so the study must be excluded.

This is a methods/protocol paper describing the counting Stroop fMRI task and summarizing validation work. It meets inclusion criteria I5 (fMRI task probing cognitive control), I6 (within-subject interference vs neutral contrast), I9 (task falls within executive function/inhibition domain), and I10 (states healthy adult sample, imaging modality, and task paradigm). However, the full text does not present original group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps or coordinate tables/maps attributable to this specific article; instead it is largely procedural/anticipatory and cites prior validation studies. Therefore it does not satisfy I7 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map) and falls under exclusion E7 (non-empirical/methods-only paper without original human neuroimaging data). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an fMRI study using the Stroop task (an established inhibition/cognitive control executive function task) with task-based within-participant contrasts (incongruent vs congruent). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (GLM) with tables/figures of activation (conflict- and error-related ACC and DLPFC activity) and describes correction thresholds and cluster criteria. Relevant participant, imaging modality, and task details are reported in Methods. Although the sample includes first-degree relatives (one relative had schizotypal personality disorder), the study provides within-group whole-brain activation maps for healthy control participants, which satisfy the requirement for healthy adult task activations. Full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 and does not violate exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI task-based study of cognitive control/executive processes (thought/image suppression, erasing/updating, imagining) in healthy adults (mean age 25.7). The paper reports within-subject contrasts of executive-task vs an active control (free-thinking) and erasing vs suppressing, performed at the group level using whole-brain voxelwise SPM2 analyses, with results presented in tables and figures (coordinates reported). Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, not rest-only baseline, empirical human fMRI data, healthy adult sample). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (N-back working memory) in adult participants. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (2-back vs 0-back), uses whole-brain, group-level voxelwise SPM random-effects analyses with reported coordinates/figures/tables, and provides participant demographic and health-screening information (cognitively intact, clinically unaffected siblings and matched healthy controls; ages reported in the 30s). The imaging modality (BOLD fMRI) and detailed task paradigm are described. All required inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, figures, references).

Exclusion(s) met: E8 — participants are aged 50–70 years, which falls outside the review age range of 18–60. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function: working memory), I6 (within-participant contrasts: manipulation/retrieval vs maintenance and vs motor control), I7 (group-level whole-brain random-effects analysis reported), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described and illustrated), I9 (task falls within executive domain: working memory), I10 (participant age, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: None (all required inclusion criteria were reported/satisfied). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Because E8 is violated (age outside 18–60), the study must be excluded despite meeting other inclusion criteria.

This fMRI study (n-back auditory WM) investigates working memory load, an established executive function, in healthy adult participants using a task-based within-subject design. The paper reports group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (second-level SPM2), whole-brain exploratory results (reported at pFDR < .05) and ROI small-volume corrected analyses, with activation coordinates and tables/figures provided. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are clearly reported. Therefore it satisfies all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

Exclusion based on E3: the study does not provide a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map. Although fMRI contrasts (Difficult vs. Control; Easy vs. Control) and individual subject SPM t-maps were computed, group analyses were performed on manually defined VOI spatial-extent measures (percent suprathreshold voxels) using t-tests rather than a voxelwise whole-brain group map. Additionally, image acquisition covered only eight axial slices of the superior brain (not whole-brain coverage). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of an executive function — planning/Tower of London), I6 (within-participant contrasts vs an active control condition), I9 (task falls in executive domain — planning), I10 (participant age, healthy sample, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported). Therefore the study is excluded under E3.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (n-back), an established executive function. It reports within-subject contrasts (one- and two-back vs zero-back active control), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps using permutation-based cluster inference. Participant details (healthy adults aged 21–29), imaging modality (3T BOLD fMRI), and task paradigm are all clearly reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This study is a PET task-based neuroimaging experiment using a working-memory (N-back) paradigm (executive function). It reports within-participant contrasts (2-back minus 0-back active control), provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses and thresholded activation maps with stereotactic coordinates and figures, and gives participant demographics (ages, healthy control status), imaging modality (H2(15)O PET), and full methods/results/discussion. All inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper includes within-group healthy control activations (so E5 not met), reports whole-brain task activations (E3/E4 not met), uses an active control (not rest-only; E6 not met), is empirical human imaging data (E7 not met), and the healthy control subgroup falls within the adult age range (E8 not met). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (stop-signal task), an executive function domain (inhibition). It reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., StopSuccess vs StopFailure; StopSuccess vs Go with 0% stop probability) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster-level inference and reported coordinates/figures. Participant information (n=24, ages 19–26, healthy) and imaging modality (3T fMRI) and detailed task paradigm are provided. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, baseline includes active Go trials, and sample is healthy adults within 18–60. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study is an fMRI Stroop (inhibition) task and reports group-level whole-brain activation maps for healthy controls and TBI patients, with participant ages, modality, and task described. However, it does not include a within-participant contrast against an active control condition—task activation is contrasted against rest/fixation only. Additionally, the sample is not restricted to healthy adults (it explicitly includes TBI patients), which conflicts with the review’s focus on healthy adults. Therefore it violates exclusion criteria E6 (rest/fixation as only baseline) and E8 (not restricted to healthy individuals). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criterion not met: I6. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Although this is an event-related whole-brain fMRI study of executive function (interference suppression and response inhibition) with within-subject contrasts (incongruent>neutral, no-go>neutral), clear group-level whole-brain voxelwise results, coordinate reporting, and full reporting of participant demographics and healthy status, the sample includes children (ages 8–12) in addition to adults. This violates exclusion criterion E8 (studies including participants outside the 18–60 years range or not restricted to healthy individuals). Therefore the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis restricted to healthy adults. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: none (all applicable I-criteria were reported), but exclusion E8 is met because participants fall outside the 18–60 age range.

This fMRI study examines inhibitory control (go/no-go), reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (PLS) with tables/figures and coordinates, and provides participant demographics and healthy screening. However, it includes older participants aged 60–80 years, i.e., participants outside the eligible 18–60 age range for this review, violating exclusion criterion E8. Therefore, despite meeting all inclusion criteria (I5–I10), the study must be excluded because it includes participants older than 60. (a) Exclusion met: E8. (b) Inclusion met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. (c) Inclusion not met: none.)

This is a task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory in healthy adults (N=14) using a Sternberg paradigm, which falls under executive function. The study reports within-subject contrasts of the experimental (working memory) condition versus an active control task, and group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-tests) were performed and thresholded, with results reported in tables/figures. Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and full task/method details are provided. Although reporting emphasized ROIs (foci reported only within predefined ROIs), a whole-brain voxelwise group analysis was conducted, satisfying the whole-brain map requirement. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This fMRI paper investigates amygdala responses to anticipation of pain while subjects perform a Continuous Performance Task (CPT) as an active coping manipulation. Although imaging, healthy adult sample, ages, and task details are reported (I10), the study does not meet the meta-analysis requirements: (1) the primary focus is emotional/pain anticipation rather than an executive-function/cognitive-control task contrast (fails I5 and I9); (2) it does not provide a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-activation map for an executive-function contrast — results are reported as ROI-based amygdala analyses (meets exclusion E3 and fails I7/I8); and (3) there is no within-participant contrast of an executive function task versus an active control condition as required (fails I6). Therefore the study should be excluded from a meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

Although this fMRI study assesses an executive-domain task (sustained attention/CPT-IP) and reports whole-brain, group-level, within-subject activation maps for healthy participants, it also includes a clinical sample (unmedicated bipolar patients) and is not restricted to healthy individuals. Exclusion criterion E8 (studies including participants outside the age range 18–60 years or not restricted to healthy individuals) therefore applies. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI executive/cognitive control task), I6 (within-participant contrast of task vs active control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables), I9 (task falls in executive domain: vigilance/sustained attention), I10 (reports participant ages, healthy sample status, imaging modality, task paradigm). Inclusion criteria not met: none (all I5–I10 satisfied). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore exclude per E8.

This study reports task-based BOLD fMRI in healthy adults performing an N-Back working memory task (executive function). It includes within-subject contrasts (2-Back vs 0-Back active control), group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise results and reported coordinates (with correction and small-volume results), and provides participant demographics and imaging/task details. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not patient-group-only, participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI to probe an executive function (planning via the Tower of London task), reports within-participant contrasts (easy and difficult TOL conditions vs yoked active control), and presents group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM results, corrected P<0.05) with coordinates and figures. Participant details confirm healthy adult samples within the 18–60 range and imaging modality and paradigms are fully described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group only, empirical fMRI data in healthy adults). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and quality metrics, so it appears complete. Inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

Although this study meets the inclusion criteria (task-based fMRI of executive function using a working memory reading-span task, within-participant contrasts against an active baseline, group-level voxelwise whole-brain analysis reported, and participant/ imaging/ task details provided), it includes an elderly participant group (mean age 68.8, range 65–71). This violates exclusion criterion E8 (studies including participants outside the age range 18–60). Because any exclusion criterion triggers exclusion, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this fMRI study assesses working memory (an executive function) with within-subject n-back load analyses and reports group-level whole-brain activation maps, it recruited both healthy control subjects and clinical patient groups (hyperthyroid, hypothyroid, subclinical hypothyroid). The review exclusion criterion E8 disallows studies not restricted to healthy individuals. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task fMRI on executive function—working memory), I6 (within-participant contrasts across n-back levels/0-back as active control), I7 (group-level whole-brain activation maps), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described/figures), I9 (task within executive domain), I10 (participant ages, health status, imaging modality, paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none. Therefore excluded due to E8 (not restricted to healthy participants). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=19, mean age 26.6) using a task that probes emotional conflict resolution—a form of cognitive control/inhibition. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs congruent; high vs low conflict-resolution trials), group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM2) with reported MNI coordinates, and detailed methods (task, acquisition, preprocessing, and analyses). Participant health status, ages, imaging modality, and task paradigm are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, not resting baseline only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I10.

This fMRI study examines working memory (auditory N-back) in cognitively intact adults and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group and within-subject (2-back vs 0-back) contrasts with coordinates and participant/task details. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, the sample age range was 25–75 years, which includes participants older than 60 and therefore violates exclusion criterion E8 (studies including participants outside the age range 18–60). Because E8 is met, the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis despite meeting the other inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/executive function in healthy adults (working memory, response selection/conflict monitoring). The paper reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., Repeat-Unexpected vs Repeat-Expected; Refresh vs Repeat) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM with reported coordinates and ROI analyses. Participant demographics (n=16, ages 18–27, healthy, right-handed), imaging modality (3T fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are provided. The design includes active control conditions (Repeat vs Refresh) and multiple within-participant contrasts that map onto executive function domains. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplemental materials are not required. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of the Multi-Source Interference Task (MSIT) in healthy adults (mean age 30.4) that probes cognitive control/interference (an executive function). It includes within-subject contrasts (interference vs control), reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses in Talairach space with figures and tables of coordinates, and provides participant demographics, imaging modality, and task details. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because inclusion criterion I10 is not met: the full text does not report participant ages (it notes seven healthy right-handed male subjects but gives no age information). The study does meet I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function using the WCST), I6 (within-participant contrasts across 3D/2D/1D conditions), I7 (group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses reported across seven subjects), I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures and coordinates), and I9 (task assesses cognitive flexibility). No exclusion criteria were triggered (E3–E8: none). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Although this fMRI study uses a two-back verbal working-memory task and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps for both patients and healthy controls, it does not include a within-subject contrast of the executive task against an active control condition. The paradigm used blocks of 2-back stimuli contrasted with rest/fixation (with occasional motor events during rest to balance motor responses), i.e., rest is the primary baseline. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (task vs an active control) is not met and exclusion criterion E6 (rest/fixation as the only baseline without an active control) applies. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of executive-function task activations in healthy adults. It uses task-based fMRI to assess working memory (n-back), an established executive function domain (I5, I9). The paper reports within-participant contrasts of n-back levels versus a 0-back active control (I6) and provides group-level whole-brain, voxelwise activation maps and coordinates with permutation clusterwise thresholds (I7, I8). Relevant participant details (ages 22–45), healthy control sample description, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly reported (I10). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group without within-group in healthy participants, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, or out-of-range ages/restricted healthy-sample violations) are met. Thus the study is eligible for inclusion.

This PET H2[15O] study of the Tower of London (planning) meets multiple inclusion criteria for the review (see below) but should be excluded because it violates age and baseline requirements. Exclusion reasons: (E8) participants include ages up to 70 years (age range 49–70), thus not restricted to 18–60; (E6) the study uses rest/fixation as the only baseline/active control (category analysis compares task to rest) and does not include a within-participant contrast against an active control task. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (PET study of executive function/planning task), I7 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures), I9 (task is planning, an executive function), I10 (participant age, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast of the executive task relative to an active control condition). Therefore exclude.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of executive-function task activations in healthy adults. It is an empirical fMRI study employing task-based paradigms assessing executive functions (PRLT for cognitive flexibility/reversal learning and Tower of London for planning) (I5, I9). Within-subject contrasts versus active baseline conditions are reported (monetary gain/loss vs neutral baseline for PRLT; planning vs baseline and parametric difficulty contrasts for ToL) (I6). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are performed and reported (FDR-corrected maps, group ANOVAs, interaction maps), with results shown in figures and tables of activations/coordinates (I7, I8). Participant information and sample characterization (healthy control group, exclusion criteria, imaging modality, and task paradigms) are described in the methods and demographics (I10). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, absence of within-group task activations in healthy participants, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, or out-of-range participants) are violated. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI task-based study of working memory (an executive function) in healthy adult participants (ages 20–29), reporting within-subject contrasts of working memory task versus an active control task and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effect analysis in Experiment 2 and fixed-effect in Experiment 1). Whole-brain results are reported with coordinates and figures. Participant health status, ages, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigms are clearly described. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group patient contrasts, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 21–31) that manipulates working memory load (two-back vs one-back) and reports neural activations. It includes within-participant contrasts comparing the high working memory load (two-back) to the low-demand baseline (one-back), meeting the requirement for an executive-function task contrast. The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses (coordinates and activations in prefrontal cortex and precuneus) in addition to ROI analyses, satisfying the whole-brain evidence criterion. The working memory manipulation falls clearly within an established executive function domain. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, out-of-range participants) are met. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of spatial working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults, reporting within-subject contrasts (structured vs unstructured sequences) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FDR-corrected) with peak coordinates. Participant ages for imaging (21–34) are within 18–60 and sample health is reported. Imaging modality, task paradigm, and relevant methodological details are provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of working memory (n-back), an established executive function domain, with clear task paradigm and participant ages reported (means ~34.3 and 37.7 years). It reports within-participant contrasts (1-back>0-back, 2-back>0-back, 2-back>1-back) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (FSL/FLAME; Z-stat images, cluster correction) for both MDD patients and healthy control subjects. Healthy within-group activation maps are described (controls show frontal activation in contrasts), and results are reported in text/figures/tables. The baseline (0-back) is an active control condition. No exclusion criteria are met: this is not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, includes within-group healthy maps, and participants are within the adult age range. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of working memory (an executive function) with within-participant BOLD contrasts and cortex-wide (vertex/whole-brain) activation maps reported in figures, and reports imaging modality and task paradigm. However, the provided full text does not report participant age or explicitly confirm healthy sample status, so inclusion criterion I10 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered based on the available information. Therefore the study must be excluded because not ALL inclusion criteria are satisfied.

This is an fMRI study of working memory in healthy adults with within-subject contrasts and participant details reported (meets I5, I6, I9, I10). However, all group-level inferential analyses are ROI-based (caudate, DLPFC, M1, PPC) and the manuscript does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps or whole-brain coordinate tables/figures that would allow inclusion. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain group results (I7) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses reported with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I9, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: I7. Exclusion criteria met: E3.

This task-based fMRI study uses a working memory (Sternberg) paradigm (executive function domain) with within-participant contrasts (five digits vs arrows baseline). Group-level voxelwise activation analyses were performed (activated voxels identified with pairwise t tests and thresholding), and results for the healthy (normal) participant group are reported. The paper reports participant ages, confirmation of a healthy control group, imaging modality (fMRI), and task details. Although the study also includes a schizophrenia group, the healthy control within-group whole-brain activation is present and usable for meta-analysis of executive function in healthy adults. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it violates exclusion criteria E8 and E6. E8: participants include ages 50–65, thus include individuals older than the allowed 18–60 range. E6: the primary task contrasts are reported relative to a resting/fixation baseline (rest circle) rather than an active control condition; no within-participant contrast against an active control condition is provided. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function — 2-back working memory), I7 (group-level whole-brain SPM analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results and coordinates described), I9 (task is working memory, an executive domain), I10 (participant age, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast versus an active control). Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it includes clinical (severe TBI) participants and is not restricted to healthy individuals (Exclusion E8). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of working memory — an executive function), I6 (within-participant contrasts reported, e.g., 2>0 and 3>0 back), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results described with anatomical labels/coordinates), I9 (task falls within executive domain — working memory), I10 (reports imaging modality, task paradigm, and confirms healthy control sample). Inclusion criteria not met: none of the I5–I10 criteria are lacking in principle. However, because the study sample includes patients (i.e., is not restricted to healthy adults), it violates exclusion criterion E8 and must be excluded from a meta-analysis restricted to healthy adults.

This fMRI study uses an n-back working memory task (an established executive function domain) with within-participant contrasts against an active 0-back baseline, reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps and cluster coordinates (including trends analysis in the healthy control group), and provides participant age information, healthy control status, imaging modality, and task paradigm. The healthy control group’s within-group whole-brain results are reported (coordinates, clusters, figures), meeting the meta-analysis requirements for inclusion.

This is an fMRI task study of working memory that reports within-subject 2-back vs 0-back contrasts and whole-brain, group-level activation maps for both controls and patients. However, the sample is not restricted to healthy adults (it includes a clinical group of never-medicated adult ADHD patients alongside healthy controls). This violates exclusion criterion E8 (studies not restricted to healthy individuals). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI executive function task), I6 (within-participant contrast against active control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described), I9 (working memory task within executive domains), I10 (participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality, task described). Inclusion criteria not met: none (all applicable I5–I10 are satisfied). Full text appears complete.

This empirical study used task-based fMRI in healthy adults performing the Conners' Continuous Performance Test (a vigilance/inhibition executive task). The authors report within-subject contrasts (task blocks vs baseline/active control of meaningless images) and group-level voxelwise analyses (one-way ANOVA producing whole-brain t-maps and cluster-level activations). Participant age, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, baseline is active images rather than fixation-only, empirical data in healthy 18–60 y/o). Although sample size is small (n=8), this does not conflict with the stated inclusion/exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded per E4: the study reports fMRI analyses but does not present a group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map. It reports ROI-restricted activation analyses in the anterior cingulate and reports whole-brain psychophysiological interaction (functional connectivity) results, but no whole-brain task activation contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI study using a task involving cognitive control/inhibition—emotional Stroop), I6 (within-participant contrast: positive vs neutral words), I9 (task falls within cognitive control/inhibition domain), I10 (participant age, healthy status, fMRI modality, and task described). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported). Therefore excluded under E4.

This fMRI study uses a Stroop color-word interference task (an executive/inhibition task), reports within-subject incongruent vs congruent contrasts, provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates/figures, and reports participant age, healthy status, imaging modality, and task details. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, it includes participants aged 47–72 yrs (range includes >60 years), which violates exclusion criterion E8 (studies including participants outside the 18–60 age range). No inclusion criteria are unmet. Because E8 is triggered, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis despite satisfying the other inclusion criteria.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adults (N=20, aged 22–30) including an n-back working memory task (an executive function). It includes within-participant contrasts (e.g., 1+2-back vs 0-back) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps thresholded at p=0.05 FWE (figures and cluster results reported). Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigms are described. No exclusion criteria are met (whole-brain results present; not a connectivity-only or between-group-only study; active control used for n-back; healthy adults within 18–60). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusions). Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study of healthy adults performing a 2-Back working memory task with an active 0-Back control, and it reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps and relevant participant information. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 are satisfied. However, the sample age range is 20–62 years, which includes participants older than the allowed 18–60 range; this violates exclusion criterion E8. Because E8 is met, the study must be excluded despite meeting other inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

The study is an fMRI investigation of working memory manipulation (executive function domain) in healthy adults and reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked maps. However, the published fMRI contrasts are reported versus a fixation (rest) baseline: 'multisubject statistical maps for all tasks (color, angle, and dual) compared with fixation'. The meta-analysis requires at least one within-participant contrast of an executive task relative to an active control condition (I6). Because the whole-brain reported maps use fixation as the baseline (a passive baseline) and no clearly described whole-brain task-versus-active-control contrast is provided, the study violates exclusion criterion E6. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criterion not met: I6. Exclusion criterion met: E6. Therefore exclude.

This is an fMRI study of verbal working memory (an executive function domain) in healthy adults (mean age 22.8) using a task-based delayed serial recall paradigm. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (voxel-wise thresholds, cluster thresholds, stereotaxic coordinates, figures/tables). Crucially, it includes within-subject contrasts between task conditions (e.g., pooled ‘difficult’ vs ‘easy’ stimulus conditions; stimulus-condition ANOVAs and matched-samples t-tests), providing an active task-versus-task comparison rather than only fixation baseline. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task details are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

Full text is incomplete (HTML skeleton only: title/metadata present; no introduction, methods, results, or discussion). Exclusion criteria met: none (unable to determine due to missing content). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria NOT met / cannot be confirmed: I5 (no information that this is an fMRI/PET task-based executive-function study), I6 (no within-participant contrast vs active control reported), I7/I8 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinates reported), I9 (task domain not described/uncertain whether an established executive function task was used), I10 (no participant age/health status/imaging modality/task details reported). Because core article content is unavailable, I cannot verify required criteria; therefore exclude with low confidence and request full text for re-screening.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (2-back) in healthy adults (N=18, age 28±7). It reports within-subject task contrasts (2-back vs a matched control condition with nonsense characters), performs group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM2 (figures and voxelwise maps described), and provides participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (4T fMRI), and task details. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive-function task activations.

This is an fMRI study of passive viewing of violent, fearful, and neutral film clips in healthy adults. Although it reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (satisfying I7) and provides participant, health-status, and imaging details (satisfying I10), it does NOT assess an executive function or cognitive-control task (fails I5 and I9). The paradigm is passive viewing rather than an executive-domain task (e.g., inhibition, working memory, cognitive flexibility), and therefore there is no within-participant contrast of an executive function task vs an active control condition as required (fails I6). No exclusion criteria are specifically triggered. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Inclusion criteria met: I7, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: I5, I6, I9. Exclusion criteria met: none.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of executive function (N-Back working memory) in healthy adults (ages 18–55). It includes within-subject contrasts of working-memory conditions (1-, 2-, 3-Back) versus an active control (0-Back sensorimotor), and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM99) with statistical maps and region findings (figures/cluster results, SVC applied to DLPFC). Participant characteristics, imaging modality, and task paradigm are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, and baseline is an active control task. Full text content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. Therefore the study satisfies all required inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and should be included in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

Although the study provides suitable within-group, whole-brain fMRI activation contrasts for an executive function task in healthy adult controls (task-switch minus task-repeat) and reports necessary participant and task details, it includes a clinical sample (21 OCD patients) alongside healthy controls. Per exclusion criterion E8 (studies not restricted to healthy individuals), this study must be excluded from a meta-analysis restricted to healthy adults. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (within-participant contrast in healthy controls), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables), I9 (task falls under cognitive flexibility), I10 (participant age/demographics, healthy-control status, imaging modality and paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none. Exclusion criteria applied: E8 (sample not restricted to healthy individuals). Full text appears complete.

This is a methods/protocol paper (Nature Protocols) describing the emotional counting Stroop and expected fMRI effects; it does not present original group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-activation maps or reported voxelwise results. The manuscript provides task design, anticipated results, and cites prior empirical studies, but no within-paper whole-brain analyses or statistical maps are reported. Therefore it meets exclusion E7 (methods-only/non-empirical paper). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task assessing cognitive control/interference) and I9 (task falls within executive function/inhibition domain). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no within-participant reported analysis results presented in this paper), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map included), and I10 (insufficient reporting of participant demographics/healthy-sample details as original data in this paper). Conclusion: EXCLUDE due to E7; recommend consulting the cited empirical papers (e.g., Shin et al. 2001; Whalen et al. 1998) for potential eligible whole-brain results.

This study used fMRI and task-based mental calculation but was conducted in 3 patients with intractable epilepsy (not healthy adults) and the main fMRI contrasts reported are mental calculation versus rest (passive baseline). There is no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-activation map in a healthy sample. Therefore the study fails the review inclusion criteria requiring healthy adult within-participant contrasts against an active control and a group-level whole-brain map. Exclusion IDs met: E8 (participants are patients, not healthy adults) and E6 (rest/fixation was used as baseline rather than an active control). Inclusion IDs met: I5 (fMRI/PET study assessing cognitive control task) and I9 (task falls within executive function domain). Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast vs active control), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise map), I10 (no healthy-sample confirmation/participants not healthy). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of planning (Tower of London) in healthy adult participants (mean age 22.5; n=22). The paper reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., six- vs four-move problems; planning vs baseline), includes active control baseline conditions (visual and motor), and conducts group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM99) with cluster-level correction; results are reported as figures and coordinate tables. The task falls within the executive function domain (planning). Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are all reported. No exclusion criteria were met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not rest-only baseline, empirical fMRI data in healthy adults). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references, appendix).

Full text content provided is incomplete (only redirect/landing text) so core methods/results are not available. Based on available metadata: (a) Exclusion IDs met: none (unable to confirm). (b) Inclusion IDs met: I9 (task is spatial working memory, an executive function). (c) Inclusion IDs not met/uncertain: I5 (modality fMRI/PET not verifiable from provided content), I6 (within-participant contrast vs active control not verifiable), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results not verifiable), I8 (reporting format of whole-brain results not verifiable), I10 (participant ages/healthy status/imaging and paradigm details not verifiable). Because the full text is incomplete, I cannot confirm that all inclusion criteria are satisfied and therefore exclude this record pending retrieval of the complete article (set fulltext_incomplete=true).

This study is excluded because it violates key exclusion criteria for the target meta-analysis. Exclusion IDs met: E6 (the task used rest/baseline fixation as the control condition rather than an active control) and E8 (participants are not restricted to healthy adults and age range reported includes older adults well above 18–60; sample includes MCI and AD patients as well as elderly controls aged 50–83). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI study of an executive function task — working memory), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps reported), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described and displayed), I9 (task falls within executive function — working memory), I10 (participant age, health status of groups, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criterion NOT met: I6 (no within-participant contrast of the executive task relative to an active control condition — baseline was rest). Because E6 and E8 are fatal to eligibility for a meta-analysis restricted to healthy adults aged 18–60 with active-control within-participant contrasts, the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of task-switching (cognitive flexibility), a recognized executive function. It reports within-subject contrasts (switch vs. repeat trials) comparing an executive condition to an active control (repeat trials). The paper includes group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (normalized beta-maps, voxelwise t-tests; reports a significant cluster in left superior parietal lobule with coordinates), and results are described in text and coordinates. The imaging modality (fMRI), task paradigm, and participant sample (nine undergraduate students) are reported; participants are adults and implicitly healthy. No exclusion criteria are met: the study does not report only ROIs, connectivity, between-group contrasts only, resting baseline only, or non-empirical data, nor include non-healthy or out-of-range participants. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Thus it meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and none of the exclusion criteria.

Full text is incomplete (only title/metadata provided). Exclusion IDs met: none. This is an fMRI task study of cognitive control/executive function (temporal integration, working memory, strategy maintenance) in healthy adults (n=26, mean age 22.4). This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults (n=16, ages 21–33). This fMRI study used an N-back working-memory (executive) task with within-subject 2-back vs 0-back contrasts, reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise activations (coordinates/figures), and provides participant ages, healthy control status, imaging modality, and task details (meets I5–I10). This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of feature-based attentional control in healthy adults (mean age 24.3). The study is an empirical, task-based fMRI investigation of cognitive control in healthy adults (n=21, mean age 33) using the Preparing to Overcome Prepotency (POP) task. This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cognitive flexibility (task-switching) in healthy young adults, reporting within-subject contrasts (e.g., bivalent > univalent; switch > repeat) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (thresholded maps and tables/figures). This is an empirical event-related fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=14; ages 19–44) that explicitly investigates response inhibition, an established executive function domain. This study is an fMRI/NIRS investigation of spatial working memory with whole-brain, voxelwise analyses and reports coordinates; it includes healthy adult control within-group results and provides participant and task details. This is an fMRI task study of visuospatial working memory (2-back) comparing users and controls. This is an event-related fMRI study of prosaccade vs antisaccade tasks (antisaccade involves inhibitory cognitive control). This is a task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/decision-making in healthy adults. This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory updating (an executive function) in healthy adults (n=12, ages 19–34). This is an empirical fMRI study of visual working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults (ages 22–36). This is an fMRI study of working memory/attentional control (three-back task with lure vs non-lure trials), sampling healthy adults (age 18–37). This study does not meet the review population and task-domain requirements. Exclusion criteria met: E8 — the sample includes older adults with MCI and AD (not restricted to healthy adults aged 18–60). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (group-level, whole-brain task-evoked maps and voxelwise analyses are reported using GLM and Talairach transformations), I8 (whole-brain results are described and illustrated in figures/tables), I10 (participant age/education, healthy control status for the control group, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (the fMRI task assesses semantic memory/naming, not an executive function/cognitive control task), I6 (no within-participant contrast of an executive function task vs an active control condition is provided), I9 (task does not fall within established executive function domains such as working memory, inhibition, or cognitive flexibility). Because E8 is violated (participants are not a healthy adult sample within 18–60 only), the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis despite some whole-brain reporting.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adult bilinguals (mean age 25.4) that explicitly investigates language control — a form of cognitive control involving inhibition/switching. It includes within-subject contrasts comparing selection contexts (e.g., LSc vs SNc, LSc vs TSc, L2 vs L1) against active naming/control conditions. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM2 results reported in figures and coordinate tables. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (fMRI, 1.5T), and detailed task paradigms are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 and does not violate any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or resting-baseline-only design; participants are healthy and age within 18–60).

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=20, ages 19–26) using a Stroop-like task assessing attentional control/inhibition (an executive function). It reports within-participant contrasts (incongruent vs. congruent targets) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (thresholded at p<.05 FDR; coordinates and tables provided). Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group task contrasts, uses active task baselines, empirical human neuroimaging data, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult volunteers (mean age 32) that directly investigates task switching (cognitive flexibility), an executive function. It reports within-subject contrasts (switching vs non-switching; semantic-category vs overlearned sequences) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM with corrected thresholds and tabulated stereotactic coordinates and figures. Participant characteristics, imaging modality, and task paradigms are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/rest-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range/unhealthy sample) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=10, mean age 29±10) that directly contrasts executive-function-related conditions against active control conditions. The spatial attention and memory paradigm (SAMP) involves working memory/attentional demands (an established executive domain). The paper reports within-participant (task vs control) contrasts and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM with voxelwise and cluster-level thresholds; peak coordinates and activation tables are provided. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and detailed task paradigms are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, participants are healthy and within 18–60). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the report is complete for screening purposes.

Full text not accessible from provided content (redirect notice). Based on title/metadata, this is an fMRI study of verbal working memory (supporting I5 and I9). However, the full article (methods/results) is not available here, so I cannot confirm key required details: (I6) that a within-participant contrast versus an active control was performed, (I7) that group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps are reported (or coordinates/figures clearly described per I8), and (I10) participant age range and confirmation of healthy adults. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) can be confirmed as met from the available information. Therefore the study is excluded due to incomplete/full-text inability to verify inclusion criteria.
