This is a prospective task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 18–35) that includes executive-function paradigms (working memory STERN; also attention), reports within-participant contrasts versus active control conditions (e.g., NT vs CT for working memory; AL vs SC and RE vs SC for associative memory), and conducts group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (group contrast maps, voxel-by-voxel SPM2 analyses with FWE correction; ROIs derived from whole-brain contrasts with MNI coordinates). Participant health status, age range, imaging modality, and task paradigms are clearly reported. None of the exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group task activations, includes active control contrasts, empirical fMRI data in healthy adults).

This is an fMRI study of an executive (working memory) task (spatial n-back) with reward manipulations in healthy adults (mean age 21.7). It includes within-subject contrasts (3-back vs 1-back; reward vs no-reward and interactions), uses group-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses with reported thresholds and tables of coordinates, and provides participant, task, and imaging details. An active control (0-back) was used. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 29–41) using a task that engages executive processes (guessing/gambling with working-memory and decision-making demands). It includes a within-subject contrast of an executive task (guessing) versus an active control (reporting) with matched perceptual/motor demands. Analyses are whole-brain voxelwise SPM group-level maps with reported activation foci/coordinates and figures/tables. Sufficient participant, imaging modality, and paradigm details are reported. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical fMRI study using the N-back working memory task (executive function). It reports within-participant 2-back > 0-back contrasts, processed with SPM5 and second-level random-effects voxelwise analyses. Whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (reporting results within a priori DLPFC via small-volume correction) and figures/coordinates are provided for significant loci. Participants are healthy adult volunteers (sample sizes and screening described; imaging sample demographics and age were reported/controlled and referenced in Supplementary Table 5), imaging modality (BOLD fMRI) and task paradigm (N-back working memory) are clearly described. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function fMRI with within-subject active-control contrast and group-level voxelwise maps. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete.

Full text is incomplete/unavailable (content only shows a redirect/placeholder). Cannot verify core methods or results against inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met / not verifiable: I5 (fMRI/PET task assessing executive function), I6 (within-participant contrast vs active control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map), I8 (clear reporting of whole-brain results), I9 (task falls within executive function domains), I10 (participant age/healthy status/imaging modality/task reported). Exclusion criteria applied: none can be confidently applied from the provided content (e.g., E3–E8 cannot be assessed without full methods/results). Because the full text is incomplete, this study must be excluded from the meta-analysis until the complete article is obtained and re-screened.

This is an original task-based fMRI study of executive function (branching integrating working memory and attentional allocation). It reports within-participant contrasts (branching vs control, delay, dual-task) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates and statistical thresholds (tables/figures). Participants were healthy right-handed adults aged 20–28. Imaging modality (fMRI), task paradigms (working memory, dual-task, planning/branching), and participant/sample details are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group contrasts, uses active control condition, empirical data, participants within 18–60 and healthy).

Full text appears to describe a resting-state fMRI study of mild cognitive impairment and mild Alzheimer’s disease rather than a task-based executive function study in healthy adults. Exclusion IDs met: E4 (resting-state/connectivity analyses without a whole-brain task activation map) and E8 (not restricted to healthy individuals; includes patient groups). Inclusion IDs met: none []. Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (not a task-based executive function fMRI/PET study), I6 (no within-participant task vs active control contrast reported), I7 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map), I9 (tasks are not within executive function domains), I10 (insufficient/irrelevant reporting for healthy adult task paradigm). Full text provided appears incomplete (only metadata/redirect page), so fulltext_incomplete=true.

This is an fMRI study of working memory (n-back) with whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses and within-participant task contrasts (e.g., 2-back vs 0-back). It meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, the sample includes both patients with schizophrenia and healthy comparison subjects (i.e., the study is not restricted to healthy adults), which violates exclusion criterion E8 (studies not restricted to healthy individuals). Therefore the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis restricted to healthy adult executive-function activations. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: none. Exclusion criteria met: E8.

This is an fMRI study of a NoGo (inhibition) task, which is an established executive function domain. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (NoGo vs Go) and presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses for healthy control subjects (contrast images, β images, and tables/figures with coordinates). Participant information (healthy control group described, demographics referenced in Table 1), imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are reported. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing verification of criteria. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without within-group healthy contrasts, resting-only baseline, non-empirical, or out-of-range participants) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study of healthy adults using working memory tasks (delayed recognition) with event-related, whole-brain group analyses; participant ages and health status are reported. However, the paper does not present a within-participant contrast of an executive task versus an active control task condition. The reported analyses focus on task-period activity (cue, delay, probe) using main-effect-of-task maps (conjunctions) and comparisons to baseline, rather than an active control task. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 is not met, and exclusion criterion E6 applies (use of rest/fixation or baseline-only contrasts without an active control). Full text appears complete.

Exclusion: The study does not investigate an established executive function task domain (it examines auditory spatial attention reorienting in a passive listening paradigm) and does not present a within-participant contrast of an executive task relative to an active control. Additionally, the primary task contrasts are reported versus a REST (silent) baseline (i.e., rest/fixation), fitting exclusion E6. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps are reported), I8 (whole-brain results and coordinates are reported in tables/figures), and I10 (participant age, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not an fMRI/PET study of executive function/cognitive control task), I6 (no within-participant contrast against an active control condition), and I9 (task does not fall within established executive function domains such as working memory, inhibition, or cognitive flexibility). Full text appears complete for screening.

This study is excluded because it reports primarily EEG-derived connectivity analyses (PDC and graph-theoretic measures) and does not provide a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map from fMRI or PET. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (reports only connectivity analyses without an accompanying whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (within-participant contrast: congruent vs. incongruent Stroop conditions), I9 (task is Stroop — an executive/inhibition paradigm), I10 (reports participant age, healthy status, imaging modalities, and task details). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a task-activation fMRI/PET study reporting task-evoked activations), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map presented), I8 (no whole-brain activation coordinates/voxelwise maps described). Full text appears complete for screening. Therefore the paper does not satisfy required whole-brain fMRI/PET activation evidence and must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=14, age 26–42) using a covert orienting task to probe inhibition of return (IOR). The study reports within-subject contrasts (long SOA vs short SOA) to isolate IOR-related effects, and uses group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses with corrected thresholds and reports peak coordinates and figures. Participant demographics, health-status screening, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are all reported. IOR indexes an inhibitory attentional process and maps onto the ‘inhibition’ domain within executive function constructs. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, active task control, healthy adults within 18–60). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of an executive-function task (colour Stroop; inhibition) in healthy adults (N=28, mean age 20.2). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (parametric linear trend across blocks varying proportion of incongruent trials and supplementary contrasts of each incongruity level vs 0% baseline), and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates and figures (P<0.001 uncorrected). Participant details, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. The 0% incongruent blocks provide an active baseline/control condition. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not resting-state-only, participants are healthy and adult). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an fMRI study with whole-brain group-level activation maps in healthy adults (meets I7, I8, I10). However, the task is autobiographical emotion induction (irritability/happiness) rather than a canonical executive-function/cognitive-control task (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility). Therefore it does not satisfy I5 (task assessing executive function/cognitive control) nor I9 (task within established executive function domains). Although within-subject contrasts are reported, they are contrasts of emotional states rather than an executive task contrast, so I6 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (N=16, ages 19–35) directly investigating cognitive control/executive function (contextual and episodic control, task switching/conflict). The paper reports within-participant, group-level voxelwise whole-brain contrasts and factorial analyses (SPM2; voxelwise and cluster thresholds; FDR correction) and presents coordinates/figures of activations. Detailed methods, participant health/age, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigms are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of working memory (delayed item recognition for letters) in healthy adults (n=40, mean age 25.1) that reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (second-level GLM and MLM) and presents coordinates/figures of activation. The paper includes within-participant contrasts across task conditions (set-size/load comparisons and delay-period effects) that serve as active cognitive-control contrasts (low vs. intermediate vs. high WM load). Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met: the study is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task contrasts, and participants are healthy adults within the 18–60 range. The full article (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an fMRI empirical study of working memory (n-back phonological and spatial tasks) in healthy adults. It reports within-subject contrasts between executive task conditions (PWM>SWM and SWM>PWM) and task>baseline contrasts, uses group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with coordinates and thresholding described, and provides participant age, health status, imaging modality, and task details. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not rest-only baseline without active contrasts, not non-empirical, participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory control/integration (an executive function domain). It reports within-subject contrasts among task conditions (IN vs SG, MO, RO) and voxelwise group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses with coordinates and brain maps. Participant information (healthy adults, ages reported), imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are described in detail. The study therefore meets inclusion criteria I5–I10. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group only, not non-empirical, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

Although this study reports group-level whole-brain fMRI analyses and provides full participant and task details, it does not assess canonical executive function domains required by the review. The main tasks are object categorization and recognition (perceptual/memory tasks), and the mental-rotation localizer probes visuo-spatial transformation rather than an established executive domain (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility). The report does not present a within-participant contrast of an executive function task vs an active control that would meet I6/I9. Therefore it fails I5, I6, and I9 despite meeting I7, I8, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) apply. Full text appears complete.

While the study is an fMRI study of inhibition (modified RPS) in healthy adults and reports whole-brain group-level voxelwise results, it does not include a within-participant contrast of an executive task relative to an active control condition. The fMRI analyses reported are task versus rest within groups and a between-group (lose vs win) comparison; subjects were assigned to win or lose groups rather than performing both conditions within-subject. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (within-participant contrast vs an active control) is not met. Exclusion criterion E6 applies because the within-subject baseline contrasts use rest/fixation without an active control task. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criterion not met: I6. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly investigates cognitive control/conflict monitoring (ACC–PFC) during semantic retrieval (the TOT state). It contains within-participant contrasts comparing TOT versus Know and Don’t Know conditions (active task conditions), reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with corrected statistics (SPM, p<0.05 cluster-corrected), and provides participant demographics (14 healthy adults, ages 19–27), imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and task paradigm details. Thus it meets I5 (fMRI study of cognitive control), I6 (within-subject contrasts against active conditions), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/tables/figures), I9 (examines cognitive control/monitoring processes within executive function domain), and I10 (reports participant age, healthy status, modality, and paradigm). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain) in healthy adults (8 participants, ages 20–25). The paper reports within-participant contrasts of executive tasks versus matched active control conditions (REP/REP CONT, MAT/MAT CONT, REP/MAT). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM) are reported, with thresholding corrected for multiple comparisons and cluster extent criteria; results are presented as statistical maps and described in the text/tables. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigms are all reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) are satisfied. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of a sustained attention (CPT) task in healthy adults (ages 18–28) that reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (SPM) comparing task blocks to baseline. CPT falls within the review’s executive-function domain (vigilance). Methods report a within-subject contrast of active CPT versus a baseline of meaningless images (visual control), which serves as an active control condition rather than simple fixation. Relevant participant information (age, health status), imaging modality (fMRI), and task details are provided. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a within-subject task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (N=23, mean age 21.3) probing selective/object-based attention and top-down cognitive control. It reports within-participant contrasts (attend vs ignore/observe) using active control conditions, and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (conjunctions and state contrasts) with thresholding described. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. The selective attention task targets cognitive control/top-down biasing processes and thus falls within executive/cognitive-control domains relevant to the review. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task contrasts, uses active control conditions, healthy adult sample). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of inhibitory control (GO/NOGO), an executive function, with healthy adult participants (N=15, age 23–40). It reports within-subject contrasts of task events (successful Stops/NOGO) relative to baseline/Go conditions and conducts group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (Talairach normalization, voxelwise thresholds, cluster correction). Results are presented as whole-brain activation maps and described in text/tables/figures. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and task paradigm are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so full text is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports an fMRI study in healthy adults using an n-back working-memory paradigm (an executive function task) with within-subject contrasts (n-back levels vs 0-back control and parametric complexity contrasts). Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) random-effects analyses are reported and thresholded; coordinates and cluster tables are provided. Participant characteristics (healthy right-handed volunteers, sample size, matching to controls) and imaging modality (1.5T fMRI) and task details are described. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Inclusion criteria applied: I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10. Exclusion criteria applied: [].

This fMRI study includes a working-memory (n-back) manipulation (executive function domain) with within-subject contrasts (high > low WM load) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects SPM results with voxel coordinates and thresholding). Participants are healthy adults (16 males, age 22–30). Imaging modality, task paradigm, and participant details are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult participants (Experiment 1: n=12, mean age 25±3.3; Experiment 2: n=12, mean age 22±4.1) investigating top-down attentional control (zooming in/out), which the authors frame as executive/cognitive control processes. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., zooming in/out vs high-level baseline [HLB]; zooming out > zooming in; zooming in > zooming out) and performs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2; cluster- and voxel-level thresholds reported) with coordinates/tables. Task paradigm and imaging modality (fMRI) are fully described. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, resting-only baseline, non-empirical paper, or out-of-range/clinical sample). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study investigates nonspatial attention shifting (feature-based set-shifting) in healthy adults using within-subject contrasts (shifting attention vs sustained attention) and reports voxelwise group results with Talairach coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of cognitive control), I6 (within-participant contrast of executive-like task vs active control), I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/figures), I9 (task maps to cognitive flexibility/set-shifting), I10 (participants’ ages, healthy status, imaging modality, and paradigm reported). However, the study does NOT meet I7: although voxelwise group analyses were performed, imaging coverage was limited to posterior brain and cerebellum (coronal slices covering occipital/parietal/part temporal and cerebellum) and did not provide whole-brain coverage (frontal regions were not imaged), so there is no qualifying whole-brain group-level activation map. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Therefore exclude because I7 is not satisfied.

Excluded because the study includes participants outside the target population for the meta-analysis: it includes a patient group (Turner syndrome) rather than being restricted to healthy adults, and includes participants younger than 18 (age range for Turner group includes 14-year-old), thus violating exclusion criterion E8. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function — working memory tasks), I6 (within-participant contrasts across task conditions/domains and distracter vs no-distracter), I9 (tasks fall within executive function domain — working memory), I10 (participant ages, health status of control group, imaging modality and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no clear report of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical map in the main text; results are primarily ROI-based with group-average activation maps reported in supplementary figures but no clearly described voxelwise group-level statistical maps for inclusion). Because E8 is met, the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis restricted to healthy adults aged 18–60.

This fMRI study investigates voluntary suppression of thermally induced pain, reporting whole-brain group voxelwise activations and healthy adult sample details. However, the suppression condition is contrasted against rest (a passive baseline) rather than an active control task; there is no within-participant contrast of the executive/suppression task relative to an active control. Therefore it fails exclusion criterion E6 (rest/fixation as only baseline). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task engages cognitive control/inhibition), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I8 (results reported with figures/tables/coodinates), I9 (task taps an executive domain: inhibition), I10 (participant age/health, imaging modality, paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast vs an active control). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because the study reports only region-of-interest analyses (no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation maps are presented in this paper) and primarily uses task vs. fixation (rest) contrasts rather than an active control condition; additionally, the sample includes clinical participants (schizophrenia) and is not restricted to healthy adults. (a) Exclusion IDs met: E3 (ROI-only, no whole-brain results), E6 (rest/fixation used as the primary baseline for key contrasts), E8 (sample not restricted to healthy individuals). (b) Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI including working memory), I9 (task within executive function domain — working memory), I10 (reported participant demographics, healthy sample status for control group, imaging modality, and task paradigm). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast against an active control condition for the executive-task contrasts), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map presented in this full text). Thus the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and is excluded.

This fMRI study examines planning, monitoring, and rule-related cognition during driving — processes that map onto executive functions (planning, rule retrieval/maintenance). It uses within-subject contrasts (e.g., Action planning > Coasting; Monitoring traffic > Coasting; Traffic rules > Coasting) against an active baseline (coasting). Analyses were conducted with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise SPM models and peak coordinates/tables are reported. Participant demographic and health information, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are reported (20 healthy right-handed licensed taxi drivers, ages 27–59). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not connectivity/rest-only; not between-group-only; participants are healthy and within 18–60). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function activations.

Exclusion E3 met: the fMRI results are presented as individual subject activation images and ROI-based summary statistics (McNemar test across regions of interest) rather than a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical map or reported coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive function — auditory digital working memory), I6 (within-participant contrast of working memory vs an active non-working-memory control), I9 (task is working memory, an established executive domain), I10 (participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no clear group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported), and therefore I8 (acceptable reporting of whole-brain results via coordinates/figures) is not satisfied at the group/voxelwise level. Full text appears complete for decision-making. Given the lack of requisite whole-brain group-level voxelwise results, this study should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (mean age reported) that investigates mental calculation tasks engaging working memory and manipulation (executive function). It reports within-subject contrasts of calculation versus active control conditions (result-matching, letter pseudo-calculation, substitution tasks). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM and results are reported in figures/tables. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and detailed task paradigms are described. Although the final analyzed sample is small (n=5) and a fixed-effects group model was used, these aspects do not violate the stated inclusion/exclusion criteria. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical PET study that assesses executive function (counting Stroop) in healthy adult volunteers. It includes within-subject contrasts of incongruent vs. neutral (active control) Stroop conditions, reported at the group level using voxelwise whole-brain SPM analyses (results presented in tables/figures). Participant ages and healthy status, imaging modality (H2(15)O PET), and task paradigm are clearly described. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are met.

Excluded because analyses were performed exclusively using region-of-interest (ROI) approaches with no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map reported, thereby violating exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive function — working memory), I6 (within-participant contrasts of task conditions), I9 (task falls within executive function domain: working memory), and I10 (participant ages reported, healthy sample, imaging modality and task paradigm described). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results provided). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because the study does not evaluate an executive function/cognitive-control task contrast required by the review. Although it is an fMRI, task-based, group-level whole-brain study (I7) with clearly reported results (I8) and reports participant/sample/task details (I10), the primary reported analyses focus on a monetary incentive delay reward task (not an executive function task) and the manuscript does not present a within-participant contrast of an executive function task versus an active control (I5, I6, I9 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study using a 2-back working memory task (an executive function domain). It reports within-participant contrasts among task conditions (Word, Cross, Within), including direct comparisons (e.g., Cross vs Within) and percent signal changes across conditions. Group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses were performed with FDR correction and reported activations with coordinates and figures. Participants are healthy adults (ages 20–28), imaging modality and task paradigm are clearly described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, active task contrasts beyond rest are reported, healthy adult sample within range). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This fMRI study uses a task that elicits cognitive interference (semantic–prosodic conflict) analogous to Stroop-like executive control tasks, and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses contrasting incongruent (CONF) vs congruent (NOCONF) conditions. Participants are healthy adults (ages 24–38). Imaging modality (fMRI), task paradigm, behavioral results, and whole-brain statistical results are reported. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based executive function activations and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This article reports task-based fMRI of working memory (an executive function) with healthy control participants and patients. It includes within-participant contrasts of working memory tasks versus active control tasks (letter-case and form-judgment control conditions). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported (cluster- and FWE-corrected results, with coordinates/tables and figures). Participant demographics and healthy sample matching are described; imaging modality (fMRI) and task paradigms are fully detailed. Although the sample includes patients, the paper provides within-group healthy control activation maps suitable for inclusion in a meta-analysis of executive function in healthy adults. Full text content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria are met.

Although this is an fMRI study of a stop-signal (inhibition) task in healthy adults and reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., STOP vs GO, STOP-success vs STOP-fail) with participant ages and task details (meets I5, I6, I9, I10), the analyses are ROI-focused and the report does not provide a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map. The authors explicitly restricted analyses to anatomically defined ROIs and did not perform or report whole-brain group-level voxelwise results. Therefore this study violates exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) and fails inclusion criterion I7 (no group-level whole-brain map). Full text appears complete. Exclusion based on E3; included criteria met: I5, I6, I9, I10; inclusion criterion not met: I7.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory and selective attention (executive domains) in healthy adult participants. It includes within-participant contrasts of executive tasks vs an active control (STERN: NT vs CT) and attention conditions (TO vs DO), and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (group maps, z-thresholds, cluster correction). Participant health status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigms are described; demographic matching and exclusion criteria are reported (see Table 1). The paper therefore meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not violate exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group task activation maps, and uses active control contrasts). Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of executive control/dual-task processing in healthy adults (ages 19–32). It reports within-subject task contrasts (DM>SM, SM>SP) and pre/post training comparisons (Time × Group, Time × Group × Condition). The manuscript includes group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-thresholded Z-stat maps) and tables/figures describing whole-head results as well as coordinate tables, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality (3T fMRI) and detailed task paradigms are reported. Although hypothesis-driven ROI analyses are used, whole-brain results are also provided (including DLPFC increases and Time × Group whole-head maps), so the study is not ROI-only. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of executive control (color–word Stroop) in healthy adults (age 24–40). It reports within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs neutral; one-word vs four-word blocks) and group-level mixed-effects whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FLAME) with peak coordinates in tables and ROI follow-ups. Participant characteristics, imaging modality, and task paradigm are fully described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group only, not non-empirical, participants are healthy and within 18–60). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This study is an fMRI task-based investigation with whole-brain group analyses in healthy adults (12 males, age 18–30). However, the paradigm primarily investigates imitation/perception–action matching and social-cognitive processes rather than a canonical executive function task. Although the authors discuss working memory and error-detection, the task does not clearly fall within established executive-function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation) as required by I9. Therefore it fails I5 (assessment of executive function/cognitive control) and I9 (task within established executive domains). Consequently I6 is not met because the within-participant contrasts are not contrasts of an identified executive function task vs an active control. The paper does meet I7, I8, and I10 (whole-brain group analyses, coordinates/tables reported, and participant/sample/imaging details provided). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults (ages 18–28). It reports within-subject contrasts between binding conditions and an active single-item non-binding baseline, conducts group-level, whole-brain (second-level voxelwise) analyses (with FDR correction), and presents whole-brain results in figures/tables. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are clearly reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it includes participants outside the eligible age range (subjects aged 18–80), thereby meeting exclusion criterion E8. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (PET study of cognitive tasks), I6 (within-participant contrasts: task minus active sensorimotor control), I7 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM and voxel-wise maps), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described and illustrated), I9 (includes executive function task: WCST; RPM contains a working-memory/abstract reasoning component), and I10 (reports participant ages, healthy sample screening, imaging modality and task paradigms). Inclusion criteria not met: none. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Because inclusion criteria are otherwise satisfied but participant age range violates the review’s 18–60 restriction, the study must be excluded per E8.

This is a within-subject, task-based fMRI study in healthy young adults reporting whole-brain group-level (random-effects SPM) voxelwise contrasts. Tasks include spatial working memory and sustained spatial attention (established executive domains). The authors report within-participant contrasts of each executive task delay period versus an active control delay, as well as laterality contrasts, with whole-brain statistics and peak coordinates. Participant demographics (n=18, mean age 23.4, healthy, non-smokers), imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigms are described in detail. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, active control used, empirical fMRI in healthy adults within 18–60).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory updating (an executive function) in healthy adults (N=16, ages 19–34). The design includes within-subject contrasts (update vs. hold; rule vs. number updates) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction; whole-brain results and coordinates are reported (supplemental tables). Participant health, age range, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm are described. The task falls squarely within the working memory/executive function domain. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cognitive control/executive function (context representation and maintenance, selection) in healthy adults (N=16, ages 21–34) using the missing-letter task. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (context vs neutral; context-appropriate vs context-inappropriate; high vs low selection demand) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported activations and coordinates. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults explicitly comparing deceptive (lie) vs truthful responses and false vs true recognition. Deception contrasts (Lie vs Truth) constitute within-subject executive/cognitive-control task contrasts, analyzed at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise random-effects statistics and reported coordinates/thresholds. Participants are healthy adults (n=20, age range 19–28). Imaging modality, task paradigm, and participant health/age are all reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This fMRI study directly assesses executive-control processes (inhibition/conflict monitoring) in healthy young adults using task-based paradigms (Piaget-like interference task vs control). It reports within-subject contrasts comparing the executive (INT) condition to an active control (COV) and uses reference control tasks (REFINT/REFCOV), computing group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g. [(INT−REFINT)−(COV−REFCOV)]), with tables/figures and coordinate reporting. Participant demographics (n=9, mean age 23.2, healthy, right-handed), imaging modality (fMRI) and detailed task methods are provided. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults (n=19, mean age 24.9) using task-based antisaccade paradigms that probe response inhibition and volitional saccade generation (executive control domain: inhibition). The paper reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., main effect of inhibition: Conditions 1 & 3 > 2 & 4; main effect of generation; interactions) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses conducted with SPM5 (FDR-corrected results and exploratory uncorrected maps). Whole-brain results are presented in tables/figures with coordinates. Participant demographics, healthy status screening, imaging modality (fMRI 1.5T), and full task methods/results/discussion are provided. Thus inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 22–25) using a delayed matching-to-sample paradigm that probes mismatch/conflict processing (working memory/executive function). The study reports within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs congruent) and group-level whole-brain analyses (Talairach normalization, group composite maps, cluster-filtered voxelwise contrasts with thresholding and figures), and provides participant demographics, imaging modality, and task details. All required information for inclusion is present and no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, uses active control conditions, healthy adult sample within 18–60). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (15 right-handed women, age 18–31) using a delayed-response working memory task with emotional, neutral, and scrambled distracters (working memory = executive function). The study reports within-subject contrasts (emotional vs neutral vs scrambled distracters; correct vs incorrect trials) and trial-based analyses. Group-level, random-effects voxelwise analyses are described and peak coordinates and t-values are reported (whole-brain maps/coordinates reported), and conjunction analyses identify inferior frontal cortex regions; results are reported as coordinates and figures. Necessary participant, modality, and paradigm details are provided. No exclusion criteria are met: this is not ROI-only, not only connectivity/rest, not between-group only, not non-empirical, and participants are within the 18–60 healthy range. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, Conclusion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cued task-switching (executive function: cognitive flexibility). It reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., task switch vs task repeat) and other condition contrasts (CTI100 vs CTI2000). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (one-sample t-tests of contrast maps, z-score maps) are described; ROIs were derived from these whole-brain contrasts. Participant details (N=22 measured, 18 analyzed after exclusions; ages 21–35; healthy) and imaging modality (3T fMRI) and task paradigm are reported. Thus all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; includes within-group contrasts; active task contrasts beyond rest; empirical data; healthy adult sample within 18–60). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study includes a task-based fMRI Stroop color-word interference experiment (an inhibition executive function task) with within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs. neutral). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (activation maps at corrected P < 0.001), and results are described in the text and figures. Participants were healthy adults aged 23–29. Imaging modality (fMRI), task paradigm, and participant details are reported. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for executive-function task activations in healthy adults and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (executive function domain) with healthy adult participants (ages 18–33). The design includes within-subject contrasts (Remember Face/Remember Scene vs Remember Both) and other within-participant contrasts; group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (one-sample t tests, conjunctions, ANOVAs) with peak coordinates and figures. The paper reports participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm in detail. No exclusion criteria are violated. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it is complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that directly assesses executive control (color-word Stroop; emotion-word Stroop) and reports within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs neutral; negative vs neutral). Group-level, voxelwise paired t-test maps were generated and thresholded (whole-brain analysis described, with cluster correction via AlphaSim), and results are presented in figures and ROI/coordinate-based analyses. Participants are healthy, ages reported (mean 18.57 years), imaging modality and task paradigms are described in detail. All required information for inclusion (I5–I10) is present. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are met: the study does not report only ROI or connectivity analyses, includes whole-brain task activation maps, uses active control (neutral word blocks) rather than fixation-only baseline, and samples healthy adults within the 18–60 range. Inclusion criteria applied: [I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10]. Exclusion criteria applied: [].

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of proactive interference resolution, a form of executive control/inhibition. It reports within-subject contrasts among task conditions (I-PI vs N-PI; C-PI vs N-PI; I-PI vs C-PI), uses group-level voxelwise SPM99 random-effects analyses with whole-brain multiple-comparison thresholds (and reports activation maps and a table of coordinates), and provides participant age range, healthy status, imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and detailed task paradigm. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants using an n-back working memory task (executive function) with within-subject contrasts (2-back vs 1-back). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported (tables/figures; corrections for multiple comparisons), and the paper explicitly reports the fMRI methods, participant ages and health status, and task paradigm. The 1-back condition serves as an active control, satisfying the within-participant active-control contrast requirement. The study also reports whole-brain interaction effects (visibility × load) localized to LOC. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria (E3–E8) apply.

This is an fMRI task study of working memory with emotional distraction in healthy adults (female, 18–33). It uses a within-subject task contrast (emotional vs. neutral vs. scrambled distracters), reports group-level random-effects whole-brain voxelwise analyses (conjunctions, maps, figures, and ROI follow-ups), and provides participant demographics and imaging protocol. The working memory task falls within executive function. Thus all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) in healthy young adults. It uses within-subject, within-participant contrasts comparing a face working-memory condition to an active sensorimotor control, and contrasts for encoding vs retrieval and memory delay vs control delay. Analyses are voxelwise/whole-brain with reported statistical thresholds, Talairach coordinates, regional volumes, and group-level effects; results are described in text/tables/figures. Participant status (healthy), imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are described; age is described as “young” (n=7). Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, resting baseline only, non-empirical, or non-healthy/out-of-range participants) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive-function task activations in healthy adults.

This fMRI study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It uses task-based fMRI (I5) with a letter-fluency task that is an established executive function paradigm (I9). The design includes within-participant contrasts of experimental versus active baseline conditions (letter fluency: word generation vs repeating the word ‘rest’; confrontation naming: naming vs fragmented picture/repeat ‘rest’) satisfying I6. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (median activation maps, non-parametric permutation testing, cluster-level statistics), and results are presented as whole-brain maps and coordinate tables (I7, I8). Relevant participant information is reported: healthy control group characteristics, age-matching, confirmation of healthy status, imaging modality (1.5T fMRI) and task paradigms (I10). Although the study includes a patient group, within-group median activation maps across subjects were computed and thresholded, providing healthy-adult task activation data suitable for inclusion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 24–33) using a counting Stroop (inhibition) paradigm. The paper reports within-subject I–N (interference vs neutral) contrasts and between-condition contrasts (Trp vs placebo). Group-level mixed-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (Z thresholds, cluster significance) and results are reported with tables/figures and peak coordinates. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm are fully described. The neutral condition serves as an active control. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This fMRI study assesses working memory (2-Back) in healthy middle-aged adults and reports group differences in task activation, but analyses were conducted using a priori ROI-based measures rather than reporting group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (within-participant contrast: 2-Back vs 0-Back active control), I9 (working memory is an executive function), I10 (detailed participant age/health, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no evidence of a group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation map; results are ROI-based). Exclusion criterion triggered: E3 (study reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis that requires whole-brain group-level maps.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain) that uses a within-subject contrast (structured vs. unstructured sequences) constituting an active control condition. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FDR correction and tabulated/figure coordinate results. Participant details (ages 19–37, healthy, right-handed, sample sizes), imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm are all clearly described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study used a task-based emotional Stroop paradigm requiring selective attention/inhibitory control (an executive function). It reports within-subject contrasts (negative vs. neutral; positive vs. neutral) using an active control (neutral words) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-thresholding and coordinates. Participants are healthy adults (college sample, mean age 18.7), imaging modality is fMRI, and task details are fully described. Thus it satisfies I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (Sternberg task) in healthy adults (mean age 24.8). It includes within-subject contrasts (e.g., ss5>ss2), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise random-effects analyses (SPM5) with coordinate tables and figures, and provides participant, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task details. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are met. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This study reports task-based fMRI of an executive control task (counting Stroop) with a within-participant contrast (incongruent > congruent) computed per individual and analyzed with group-level, whole-brain random effects voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with reported coordinates and figures. The task is a canonical inhibition executive function paradigm. Relevant participant information (ages, healthy control inclusion/exclusion criteria), imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that explicitly tests cognitive control/conflict (ACC, DLPFC) during moral dilemmas. It includes within-subject contrasts isolating control demands (high-RT vs low-RT personal dilemmas; utilitarian vs nonutilitarian trials with RT matched), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (with thresholds and cluster correction), and provides participant demographics (41 healthy adult undergraduates), imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm details. The tasks probe inhibition/cognitive control processes, which fall within executive function domains. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, uses task contrasts beyond fixation, empirical human neuroimaging with healthy adults). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI, task-based working memory study with within-participant contrasts and group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (see reported Talairach coordinates and voxelwise thresholds). It therefore meets I5 (fMRI executive-function task), I6 (within-participant contrasts against active distracter baseline/control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I8 (coordinates/voxel reporting), and I9 (working memory task within executive domains). However, the full text as provided does not report participant ages (it states only “six right-handed normal participants”), and Inclusion criterion I10 requires relevant information about participant age in addition to healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm. Because participant ages are not provided, I10 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded due to failure to meet I10 (participant age reporting).

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) that includes within-participant contrasts (e.g., switch vs. stay cues and cue-related contrasts), group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with FDR correction, and reports whole-brain results in tables/figures. The task falls squarely within executive-function domain (working memory). Participant demographics (ages within 18–60), healthy sample status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, resting-only baseline, non-empirical, or out-of-range/unhealthy samples) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI empirical study of verbal working memory (an executive function domain). It includes within-subject contrasts (MEMORY [EAR/EYE] vs NO-MEMORY active control), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (surface-projected group t-statistic maps, thresholds and cluster criteria reported), and reports coordinates/results in the text/figures. Participant information is provided (16 healthy adults, ages 20–42), imaging modality (3T fMRI) and detailed task paradigm. Thus it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not limited to ROIs, not only connectivity, not between-group patient contrasts, include an active control (NO-MEMORY), are empirical with healthy adults within 18–60. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of selection (response selection/free choice) in healthy adults (n=12, age 23–38). It reports within-subject, group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., free selection vs externally specified; action vs colour) with SPM results and coordinate tables/figures, and provides full methods, results, and discussion. Tasks target executive selection/cognitive control processes. Participant health, ages, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study reports fMRI of a verbal working-memory (delay) task in healthy adults and provides group-level whole-brain activation results and participant/task details, but it does not present a within-participant contrast of the executive task against an active control condition. The reported maps appear to reflect task-evoked activations relative to fixation/baseline (or simple task epochs) rather than an active control condition, which violates exclusion criterion E6. Therefore I cannot include it for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI event-related study of pro- and anti-saccades (anti-saccades are an inhibition/cognitive-control task), but the primary analyses are ROI/time-course based using single-subject localizer maps and extracted FEF/SEF/IPS time courses rather than a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map. Inclusion met: I5 (fMRI task involving cognitive control—anti-saccades), I6 (within-participant contrasts and analyses comparing pro- vs anti-saccades and SRT quartiles), and I9 (task falls within executive domain: response inhibition). Inclusion not met: I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical map for the main executive contrasts reported; the localizer/ROIs were single-subject and main results are ROI-based), I10 (participant age information is not clearly reported). Exclusion applied: E3 (results rely on ROI/extracted time-course analyses with no qualifying whole-brain group map). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of working memory (n-back) and attention tasks (executive domains). It reports within-subject contrasts between task levels (1-back,2-back,3-back) and intertask contrasts (e.g., 2-back vs 1-back, 3-back vs 2-back), providing active control comparisons. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps and thresholding procedures are described, and within-group main effect maps for healthy controls are reported. Participant ages (controls: 23–50; patients: 22–49) are within 18–60, healthy control status is confirmed, imaging modality and task paradigms are detailed. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, within-group healthy participant activations are present, and an active task control (lower-load n-back) is used. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Thus the study meets all specified inclusion criteria for executive-function task activations in healthy adults and can be included.

This is an fMRI study with group-level whole-brain analyses and reports participant/sample and imaging details (I7, I8, I10 satisfied). However, the task is a smooth pursuit oculomotor paradigm (target tracking with blanking) and not an established executive function or cognitive control task (does not meet I5 or I9). Although there is a within-subject contrast (target blanking vs continuous), that contrast does not assess an executive function relative to an active control (I6 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are directly triggered by the study. Therefore it must be excluded because it fails to meet the required inclusion criteria for executive function task relevance (I5 and I9).

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults (N=17, age 20–40) that investigates antisaccade performance (inhibition and volitional generation), which clearly falls within executive function (inhibition) domains. The study reports within-subject contrasts (antisaccade vs prosaccade; phase-wise inhibition vs generation) using group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses in SPM2 and presents voxelwise results (figures and Table 2 coordinates) with cluster-corrected thresholds. Relevant participant, modality, and task details are reported. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60 years. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and none of the exclusion criteria.

This study reports task-based fMRI (N-back working memory) in healthy adult participants using a within-participant 2-back vs 0-back contrast, with group-level voxelwise analyses in SPM99 and coordinates/vouchered loci reported for prefrontal activation. Participant characteristics (adults 18–60, healthy controls/subgroup matched for age, handedness, IQ) and imaging modality/task paradigm are described. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (fMRI executive function task), I6 (within-participant contrast vs active control), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analysis), I8 (coordinates/figures reported), I9 (working memory = executive domain), and I10 (participant age/healthy status/imaging modality/task reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group healthy activation contrast, uses active control). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This fMRI study examines sustained attention (psychomotor vigilance task), an accepted executive-function domain (vigilance). It reports within-participant contrasts (fastest vs intermediate RTs and task-related effects) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (tables/SOM referenced). Participants are described as young healthy adults, imaging modality (fMRI) and task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task contrasts, does not use rest-only baseline as the sole contrast, is empirical, and samples healthy adults). Full text contains methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a verbal fluency paradigm (an established executive/frontal task) with within-subject contrasts of correct task performance versus an active control (‘rest’ word aloud). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (activation maps, cluster coordinates, and figures). Healthy control within-group activation maps are provided, and participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality (fMRI) and task paradigm are described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group healthy activations). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although the study meets the methodological inclusion criteria (fMRI task-based executive paradigms, within-participant task vs active control contrasts, whole-brain voxelwise group analyses with coordinates reported, tasks within executive-function domains, and adequate participant/age/imaging/task information), it includes a clinical sample (participants with Autism Spectrum Disorder) alongside healthy controls. This means the study sample is not restricted to healthy individuals, which violates exclusion criterion E8. Therefore the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis limited to healthy adults. Inclusion IDs met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion IDs not met: none. Exclusion IDs met: E8 (study includes non-healthy participants).

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 18–36) that includes the emotional counting Stroop, a task assessing cognitive control/interference (inhibition), satisfying the executive-function domain. The Stroop analyses use within-participant contrasts (positive vs. neutral; threatening vs. neutral) and are reported as group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps with cluster thresholds and peak MNI coordinates. Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality, and task paradigms are fully reported. The facial expression task is non-executive but unnecessary since the Stroop fulfills the executive-function requirement. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; whole-brain results are presented; not connectivity/rest-only; includes within-group task contrasts; sample restricted to healthy 18–36-year-olds). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 are met.

This is an fMRI task-based study of executive function (attention switching within verbal working memory) in healthy adults (N=11; ages 19–41). The authors performed within-subject contrasts parametrically manipulating switching frequency (High/Medium/Low) and report group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (voxelwise repeated-measures ANOVA) with tables/figures of significant clusters (Tables 2–3, Fig.3) and Talairach coordinates. Task falls within established executive domains (working memory/attentional control). Participant characteristics, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, includes active within-task contrasts beyond rest, empirical human neuroimaging, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and is eligible for inclusion.

This is an event-related fMRI study of saccadic inhibition (antisaccade task), an executive-function (inhibition) paradigm. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (ANT and FIX vs PRO) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (with Bonferroni correction), including figures and Talairach coordinates for activation peaks. A healthy control group is reported (n=17, mean age 25.9 ±4.1) with within-group activation information described; imaging modality, task paradigm, and participant ages/health status are all reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, or age/healthy-sample violations) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and is appropriate for inclusion in a meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) in healthy adult participants. It reports within-subject contrasts (selection vs. neutral cue) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2 one-sample t-tests and regression), with results described and peak coordinates/thresholding provided in tables and figures. Participant age and healthy status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are all reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, uses an active control cue rather than only rest/fixation, is empirical, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of working memory/interference resolution in healthy adults with within-participant task contrasts (meets I5, I6, I9, I10). However, the paper reports ROI-based analyses derived from individual subject task-effect contrasts and reports percent signal change within ROIs rather than presenting a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or coordinates/tables of whole-brain results. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study of an executive function task (working memory recency-probes) with within-subject contrasts of interference vs noninterference. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM results are reported (tables of coordinates, cluster thresholds, and conjunction analyses), and the paper provides participant characteristics (n=27, adults 18+), confirms healthy participants, specifies imaging modality (3T fMRI), and details the task paradigm. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/executive processes (letter vs visuospatial decision tasks) in healthy adult volunteers. It reports within-subject contrasts (letter vs visuospatial; tasks vs baseline) using an active control baseline (simple reaction-time task), and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates and corrected statistics. Tasks probe executive functions (response selection, inhibition, conflict monitoring). Participant sample is described as healthy right-handed volunteers (n=16); imaging modality (fMRI) and task paradigms are clearly reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of executive function with within-participant contrasts and whole-brain maps.

The full text reports a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (mean age 24.6) that directly probes working memory and recognition processes (an executive function domain). The within-subject contrasts include game > dot (a working-memory vs. perceptual-motor active control), game > scene, and game > random. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise SPM analyses (fixed-effects) were performed and significant clusters are reported (tables/figures and coordinates), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. Participant, imaging modality, and task details are provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria relevant to this meta-analysis are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI task-based study of verbal working memory (an executive function). It uses within-subject contrasts of maintenance versus an active case-judgment control, reports group-level whole-brain analyses (random-effects t maps and coordinates) and functional connectivity, and provides participant demographics (11 healthy adults, mean age 21.4). Thus it satisfies I5–I10. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, uses an active control, empirical fMRI study with healthy adults). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults that includes within-subject, whole-brain, voxelwise contrasts that probe cognitive control/executive processes during an empathy/perspective-taking task. Although the primary topic is empathy for pain, the authors explicitly test and interpret contrasts (e.g., No Pain: Dissimilar > Similar) in terms of executive functions such as response inhibition and self–other distinction (rIFC, dmPFC), and perform whole-brain random-effects analyses with reported coordinate tables. Participant age and healthy status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are fully reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task contrasts, uses active task controls, empirical data in healthy 19–34 year-olds). Therefore it meets the meta-analysis requirements for inclusion of executive-function-related task activations.

This study must be excluded because it includes participants outside the eligible age range (13-year-old children in addition to adults), meeting exclusion criterion E8. The study otherwise satisfies the inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI of an executive function — visuospatial working memory), I6 (within-participant contrasts comparing WM events to control trials), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with corrected results and reported coordinates), I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables and text), I9 (task falls within executive function — working memory), and I10 (reports participant ages, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm). No other exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Inclusion criteria not met: none (all I5–I10 met). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded solely due to E8.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E8 — the study includes clinical participants (bipolar disorder) and is not restricted to healthy individuals, despite inclusion of a healthy control group. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI Stroop, an executive/inhibition task), I6 (within-participant contrast: incongruent vs congruent trials), I7 (group-level, voxelwise whole-brain composite maps and voxelwise t-statistics reported), I8 (results reported in figures and described in text), I9 (Stroop falls within inhibition/executive function), I10 (participant ages and healthy control status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: none – all applicable inclusion criteria were satisfied for the control-task activation. However, because E8 applies, the study must be excluded per the protocol (it is not restricted to healthy adults). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults assessing attention/alertness (vigilance), which falls within executive function domains. It reports within-subject contrasts between two active task conditions (distributed vs focused spatial attention) and performs whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM second-level random effects) with coordinates/tables and figures. Participant age range and health status, imaging modality, and task paradigms are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, resting-only baseline without active task, non-empirical, or out-of-range/clinical samples) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This PET study of the PASAT in healthy adults meets all inclusion criteria for an executive-function activation meta-analysis. It uses task-based PET imaging assessing executive processes (working memory/attention) (I5), includes within-participant contrasts of the executive task versus active control tasks (PASAT–repeat immediate, PASAT–repeat prior; I6), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses with coordinates and corrected p-values (I7, I8). The task falls within established executive domains (working memory/attention; I9). The paper reports participant ages, confirms a healthy sample, specifies imaging modality (PET), and details the task paradigm (I10). Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is provided and appears complete.
