This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults using a go–nogo paradigm (response inhibition), meeting the executive function domain. It reports within-subject contrasts (nogo vs go) and group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses (conjunction and interaction), with coordinates and statistical maps described in text and figures. Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality, and task details are all reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, active control present, empirical human imaging in healthy adults). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, Conclusion).

This is an empirical PET study of spatial working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults. It uses task-based within-subject contrasts (spatial span and spatial manipulation vs matched visuomotor control) and reports group-level voxelwise analyses using SPM96 with whole-brain exploratory searches and stereotaxic coordinates (Table 1, figures). Participants are healthy right-handed adults aged 44–55. Imaging modality (PET), task paradigms, participant details, and statistical whole-brain results (coordinates and mapped images) are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although the study uses fMRI, a within-participant task vs active control contrast, reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results, and tests a healthy adult sample with ages reported, the experimental task (Word Memory Test delayed recognition) is an episodic/declarative memory retrieval task rather than an executive function or cognitive-control task as required (I9). Therefore it does not meet the key inclusion criterion that tasks fall within established executive function domains. Full text is complete and exclusion criteria E3–E8 do not apply. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task not clearly assessing executive function/cognitive control), I9 (task not within listed executive-function domains). No exclusion criteria were triggered.

This study used fMRI in healthy adult samples and analyzed task data (including 3-back working memory) with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps, and reports results clearly — satisfying I5, I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, the presented analyses focus on trial-by-trial RT regressors and task-vs-fixation contrasts (fixation baseline), and I find no within-participant contrast of an executive function task relative to an active control condition (e.g., 3-back vs 0-back or another active control). Therefore I6 is not met. Because the study appears to use fixation/rest as the baseline for task-related contrasts without reporting an active control contrast, exclusion criterion E6 applies. Conclusion: EXCLUDED for failing to meet I6 (and triggering E6).

This is an fMRI study of working memory (source vs picture tasks) in healthy young adults and reports within-subject task contrasts and participant/sample details (meets I5, I6, I9, I10). However, the authors restricted analyses to a mask of regions taken from a prior study and report percentage signal change in those ROIs; no group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps are presented. Therefore the paper appears to report only ROI-based analyses and does not provide whole-brain results, violating inclusion criterion I7 and meeting exclusion criterion E3. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

Although this fMRI study reports whole-brain, group-level, within-subject contrasts and provides participant demographics and imaging details, it does not examine a task that falls within the review's specified executive function domains. Met: I5 (fMRI task-based study addressing cognitive control/conflict), I6 (within-participant contrasts: Magic vs Causal Control; Surprise vs Causal Control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (results reported as coordinates/tables and described), I10 (participant age, healthy sample status, modality, and task paradigm reported). Not met: I9 — the paradigm involves perception of magic tricks and violations of causal expectation (a perceptual/reasoning paradigm probing disbelief/conflict detection) rather than established executive function tasks (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). The authors interpret activations in terms of conflict/cognitive-control, but the task was not designed or categorized as a canonical executive function task. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) were triggered. Therefore the study is excluded for failing I9.

This is an empirical, within-subject fMRI study of a go–nogo paradigm (inhibition/conflict) in healthy adults (ages 19–60). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FSL FLAME, cluster thresholding) with coordinates and figures, and includes within-participant contrasts relevant to executive function (go vs nogo; compatibility and co-action vs single-actor interactions). Imaging modality, sample demographics/health, and task details are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, uses active task baselines, empirical with original human neuroimaging data, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this study is a task-based fMRI investigation of sustained attention (vigilance) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses in a healthy control sample, it does not include an active control condition for the required within-participant task vs active-control contrast. The task contrasts are reported primarily against a fixation baseline and practice (novel vs. practice) repetitions; therefore the study uses rest/fixation as the primary baseline rather than an active control. This violates exclusion criterion E6 and fails inclusion criterion I6 (no within-participant contrast against an active control). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of an executive domain—vigilance), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group analyses), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables), I9 (task falls within executive function domain—vigilance), and I10 (participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no within-subject contrast against an active control).

Full text is not accessible (only a redirect/placeholder page shown), so core article content (methods, results) cannot be verified. Therefore I cannot confirm that the study meets the required inclusion criteria. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none (cannot verify). Inclusion IDs not met / not verifiable: I5 (cannot confirm it is an fMRI/PET task assessing executive function), I6 (cannot confirm within-participant contrast vs an active control), I7 (cannot confirm group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I8 (cannot confirm coordinate/figure whole-brain reporting), I9 (cannot confirm tasks fall within defined executive domains), I10 (cannot confirm participant age range, healthy status, imaging modality and task paradigm). fulltext_incomplete=true.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of working memory (N-back), an executive function task, in healthy adults. It reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., 2-back/4 vs 2-back/1 and conditions vs 0-back), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FDR correction, and presents whole-brain activation maps and cluster results in text/figures. Participant demographics (mean age 26.6, healthy screened) and imaging modality (3T BOLD fMRI) and task paradigm are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, inappropriate sample age/health) are met. Full article content (background, methods, results, discussion) is present, so fulltext is complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that directly manipulates executive function (working memory load) and visuo-spatial attention using task-based paradigms. It includes within-participant contrasts of high vs low load (active control conditions) and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (voxelwise), with results reported in figures and tables. Participant ages and healthy status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigms are clearly described. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, or out-of-range/clinical samples) are met. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext is complete.

This is an fMRI study of a canonical executive function (visual spatial working memory; n-back). It reports within-subject contrasts (2-back and 1-back relative to 0-back active control), and group-level voxelwise analyses identifying whole-brain activation clusters (right inferior frontal gyrus and intraparietal sulcus) derived from the 2-back vs 0-back contrast. Core article sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) and participant details (nine healthy adults aged 26–32), imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and task paradigm are reported. Although a volume-of-interest analysis was used for effect-size extraction, the regions were first identified via a whole-brain second-level contrast. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (n-back) in healthy adults (analyzed N=31, age 20–50). It reports within-subject contrasts (2-back > 0-back; verbal vs spatial) using a group-level mixed-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analysis with cluster-thresholded statistical maps and peak coordinates. Task falls within executive function (working memory). Participant, imaging modality, and paradigm details are reported. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text appears complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI task study of executive function (working memory monitoring) in healthy adults (N=13, ages 19–27). It reports within-subject contrasts (self-ordered vs recognition; externally triggered vs recognition; self-ordered vs externally triggered). Analyses were performed as group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise statistical maps with thresholding and coordinates reported. Participant characteristics, imaging modality, and task paradigm are described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI, task-based study of directed forgetting that explicitly probes intentional inhibition/cognitive control. It includes within-subject contrasts of Forget versus Remember instructions (F > R and related F_F > R_F contrasts), reported as group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with tables of coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction. The task targets inhibitory/ executive control processes (memory suppression), and participant information (healthy adults, mean age ~27), imaging modality (3T fMRI), and detailed paradigm are reported. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, or non-healthy/out-of-range ages) are met.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is an fMRI (and MEG) task-based study of working memory (an established executive function domain) in healthy young adults (I5, I9). The authors performed within-participant contrasts of encoding versus baseline/control epochs (active encoding vs control epochs) to obtain task-evoked effects (I6). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were carried out with multiple-comparison correction and results are reported in tables/figures (I7, I8). Participant age, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are clearly reported (I10). No exclusion criteria are met: the study does not restrict to ROI-only analyses (E3), is not connectivity/rest-only (E4), includes within-subject task activation contrasts in healthy participants rather than only between-group contrasts (E5), does not use only rest/fixation baseline (E6), is empirical human neuroimaging work (not E7), and participants are healthy adults within 18–60 years (not E8). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (age 19–33) examining working memory manipulation (an executive function). It includes within-subject contrasts (manipulation cue vs retrieval cue) and other within-participant contrasts. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cue minus maintenance contrast reported at p<0.05 FDR and shown in figures) and provides coordinates and descriptions of results. Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are reported. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria are met.

Excluded because the study violates exclusion criteria E6 and E8. E6: the fMRI contrasts are reported relative to a resting/fixation baseline (21 s fixation blocks) and no active control task condition is used; the main contrasts and ROI analyses compare task to baseline rather than to an active control. E8: the healthy control sample is elderly (mean age 69.1 years), outside the required 18–60 age range for the review. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function: 2-back working memory), I7 (group-level whole-brain/voxelwise maps are reported and shown in figures), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described and illustrated), I9 (task falls within executive domains: working memory), I10 (participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast against an active control condition). Because E6 and E8 are violated, the study must be excluded.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E8 — the study includes participants outside the 18–60 yrs range (breathholding group ages 11.5–24.2), so the sample is not restricted to adults 18–60. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function — verbal working memory), I6 (within-participant task vs control blocks and task-based contrasts), I9 (task falls within executive function domain — working memory), I10 (participant ages and health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I7 — the paper does not clearly present a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map (analyses appear to use per-subject voxelwise maps with group comparisons on activation volumes rather than a group voxelwise statistical map). Because E8 is met and I7 is not met, the study must be excluded for this adult executive-function meta-analysis. Full text appears complete.

Exclusion based on: E6 (study uses fixation/rest as the baseline for task contrasts rather than an active control) and E8 (study includes a clinical autism sample and is not restricted to healthy adults). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps are reported), I8 (results reported with coordinates and figures), and I10 (participant ages, imaging modality (fMRI), task paradigm, and screening of control participants are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (tasks are sensorimotor eye-movement paradigms, not clearly within established executive function domains), I6 (no within-participant contrast against an active control condition), and I9 (tasks do not fall within canonical executive function domains like working memory/inhibition/planning). Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cognitive control processes. It reports within-participant contrasts (insight vs analytic trials) that reflect differing modes of cognitive control/cognitive flexibility, uses whole-brain, group-level voxelwise GLM analyses with reported cluster coordinates, and describes imaging modality (3T fMRI) and task paradigm (CRA problems) in healthy participants. The report identifies ACC preparatory activity related to cognitive control/conflict monitoring and switching, mapping onto executive-function domain (cognitive flexibility). Participant health, modality, and paradigm are described; although precise ages are not enumerated in the excerpt, the sample is described as neurologically healthy adults. Given the whole-brain maps/coordinates and within-subject task contrasts in an executive/control-relevant paradigm, the study meets inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis.

Full text appears incomplete in the supplied content (only metadata/abstract available), preventing verification of all required inclusion criteria. From the abstract it is clear the study used PET imaging (I5 satisfied). However I6 (explicit within-participant contrast against an active control) cannot be fully confirmed—while sequences were compared to simple repetitive movement, the full methods/contrasts are not available. I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results) cannot be confirmed from the abstract. I9 (task falls within established executive function domains) is uncertain: the task is motor sequencing with suggested involvement of spatial working memory but may be primarily motor/execution rather than an executive-domain task. I10 (sufficient reporting of participant age and healthy status) is not provided in the abstract. Because the full text is not provided, I cannot verify whether any exclusion criteria (e.g., use of rest-only baseline, ROI-only analyses, non-healthy participants) are met or violated. Therefore I must exclude due to incomplete/full-text unavailable for full verification. Inclusion IDs met: I5. Inclusion IDs not met/uncertain: I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. Exclusion IDs met: none (cannot determine)." ,

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (N-Back) in healthy adults (mean age 31.8), reporting within-participant contrast (2-Back > 0-Back). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and coordinates/thresholds are reported; results are presented in text, figures, and tables. Imaging modality (BOLD fMRI), sample demographics, and task paradigm are described. Supplemental material is referenced but not required for core criteria. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (executive function) in healthy adults (n=12, mean age 24). It reports within-subject contrasts (NT vs CT, PT vs NT) using an active reaction-time control task (CT). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps are reported/thresholded and peak coordinates are provided (Table 1, figures). Methods, results, and participant details are fully described. The paradigm is a working memory automatization task and a dual-task assessing processing capacity, which fits established executive-function domains. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an empirical PET study in healthy adult bilinguals that explicitly investigates cognitive control processes (translation requiring inhibition of the dominant language and language switching requiring set-shifting/phonological recoding). It reports within-subject contrasts (translation vs reading; switching vs no-switching) using group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses with tables of coordinates. Participant ages (25–39), healthy status, imaging modality (PET), and detailed task paradigms are reported. The tasks map onto established executive function domains (inhibition, cognitive flexibility). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, uses active control baselines, empirical human neuroimaging with healthy adults aged 18–60). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Given these points, the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an event-related fMRI study of working memory (an executive-function domain) that: (1) uses a task-based paradigm probing manipulation/maintenance (WM) versus an active control condition (three Xs/button press) and reports within-participant contrasts ([load − control]); (2) reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise results and stereotaxic coordinates and figures; (3) provides sufficient participant information (healthy control group demographics, imaging modality, task details) and examines healthy controls separately; and (4) clearly falls within established executive function domains. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group healthy participant activations). Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and should be included for the meta-analysis of executive-function task activations in healthy adults.

This task-based PET study in healthy adults (n=6, ages 19–32) assesses conditional movement selection (stimulus-response mapping), a form of cognitive control/response selection. It includes a within-subject contrast of conditional versus active control tasks (conditional − (power+precision)/2), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps with peak coordinates and t-values, and provides participant demographics, healthy sample confirmation, imaging modality, and task details. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I10. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it uses fMRI to assess an executive function task (verbal 2-back working memory; I5, I9); includes within-participant contrasts of task vs an active baseline (symbol discrimination) allowing task-evoked contrast (I6); reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps and random-effects group analyses with stereotaxic normalization and correction for multiple comparisons (I7) with results presented in figures/tables (I8); and provides participant ages, healthy control status, imaging modality, and task details (I10). The healthy control group provides within-group activation maps appropriate for inclusion in a meta-analysis of executive-function activations in healthy adults. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, resting-only baseline, or age-range violations). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This fMRI study tested working memory (delayed recognition) for voice identity and location — an established executive function domain (working memory). It reports within-participant contrasts of each memory task versus an active sensorimotor control, and direct voxelwise group-level whole-brain statistical maps (Z-maps) with tables/figures and ROI analyses. Participant age (18–27), healthy status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigms are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; includes whole-brain task activation maps; not connectivity-only; includes within-group contrasts; uses an active control; healthy adult sample within 18–60). This meets exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI examining working memory, an executive function), I9 (task falls within an executive function domain — working memory), and I10 (reports participant ages, healthy sample, imaging modality, and task paradigm). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no clear within-participant contrast of an executive task versus an active control reported as a standard task activation contrast), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map), and I8 (no acceptable reporting of whole-brain results in coordinates/figures). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is excluded under E3.

This fMRI study examines working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults and reports whole-brain voxelwise results, but its control condition is passive visual fixation (subjects instructed to fixate a crosshair). Inclusion criterion I6 requires a within-participant contrast versus an active control, and exclusion criterion E6 bars studies using rest/fixation as the only baseline. Therefore the study must be excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function/working memory), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis reported via SPM and thresholding), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/tables/figures), I9 (task falls within executive function domains—working memory), I10 (participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and paradigm reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no active control; only fixation baseline). Exclusion criterion met: E6 (rest/fixation-only baseline). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an original, task-based fMRI study of working memory manipulation (executive function) in healthy adults (mean age 25, n=18). It reports within-participant contrasts (color vs angle; conjunction vs color/angle) using a group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM with voxelwise inference and cluster-size thresholding; coordinates and statistical thresholds are provided. Imaging modality (3T fMRI), participant health/age, and task paradigm details are fully reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults using the antisaccade task, a well-established inhibition/cognitive-control paradigm. It includes within-subject contrasts (antisaccade vs prosaccade; correct vs error) and reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain GLM analyses with corrected thresholds and stereotaxic coordinates. Participant demographics (mean age, healthy status), imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are reported. All required inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because the sample includes participants aged 37–83, i.e. includes individuals older than 60, violating exclusion criterion E8. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (PET task-based study of executive/cognitive-control processes using semantic and syllable decision tasks), I6 (within-participant contrasts vs an active control condition — semantic vs syllable), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described/figured), I9 (tasks map onto executive domains: working memory/monitoring/decision-making), I10 (participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none (all applicable I5–I10 satisfied). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded solely due to E8 (age range outside 18–60).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults using n-back working memory tasks (1-back, 2-back), which are established executive function paradigms. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., 2B vs PL, 1B vs 2B) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FLAME mixed-effects, cluster-corrected Z maps) with tables of local maxima and figures. Participant ages (22–31), healthy status, imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and task details are provided. Thus all required inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults with group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and within-subject contrasts, it does not target established executive function domains. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (within-participant contrasts: introspection vs categorization; rapid vs slow), I7 (group-level whole-brain random-effects maps reported), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/figures), I10 (participant age, healthy sample, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (study does not assess executive function or cognitive control per se; focuses on self-related introspection and sensorimotor categorization), I9 (tasks do not fall within established executive function domains such as working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Therefore the study should be excluded from this meta-analysis.

This is an event-related fMRI study of a working memory (Sternberg delayed face recognition) task in healthy adults (ages 22–27), meeting the review objective of executive function activations. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (match vs nonmatch) during the response period and reports both ROI and a whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analysis (Talairach-normalized t maps, voxelwise thresholding), with coordinates and anatomical descriptions. Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are all reported. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (appears complete). Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, participants are healthy and within age range).

The study is an fMRI task study of infrequent target detection (an oddball task interpreted as engaging working memory/attention) with a within-subject contrast of targets versus standards and reports participant ages and healthy status. However, the imaging coverage was limited to four coronal slices (partial-brain coverage) and the reported group analyses do not constitute a whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map as required by I7. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I9, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise results). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI task study of subliminal motor inhibition in healthy adults (age 27–34) addressing inhibition (an EF domain) with within-subject contrasts (compatible vs incompatible). However, although the authors ran whole-brain analyses they report no significant whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked results and present significant findings only from ROI analyses. Because the study effectively reports only ROI results with no whole-brain activation map/peaks to include in a voxelwise meta-analysis, it fails the requirement for usable group-level whole-brain task activation evidence. Therefore exclude under E3. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that examines decision uncertainty and cognitive control during a prototype distortion categorization task. It reports within-participant contrasts (parametric modulation across distortion levels; untrained > trained) using whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM5) with FDR correction and provides coordinate tables and figures. Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality, and task details are reported. The paradigm engages executive processes (conflict monitoring, response selection, working memory/attention demands and training-related cognitive control changes), fitting the meta-analysis focus on executive function activations. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, or unhealthy/out-of-range samples) are met.

This fMRI study examines executive processes (relational reasoning/working memory) in healthy adults (n=8, ages 19–32). It reports within-subject contrasts including parametric complexity vs distractor conditions and a direct subtraction of high-complexity minus high-distractor (an active control), fulfilling an executive-task vs active-control contrast. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise maps (SPM99) reported in figures/tables with coordinates and thresholds. The paper reports participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and detailed task paradigm. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (E3–E8) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of object naming/semantic context and visual feature effects, not an executive function or cognitive control task in established EF domains (e.g., working memory, inhibition, set-shifting). Although it reports within-participant contrasts (homogeneous vs. heterogeneous naming) and whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates and participant details, the task does not target executive function per inclusion criteria. Thus I5 (study assessing executive function) and I9 (task within established executive function domains) are not met; I6 (within-participant contrast of an executive function task vs active control) is therefore not satisfied. Full text is complete. Exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are not triggered.

This PET study reports task-based, within-subject contrasts that isolate cognitive components of motor sequence learning (explicit spatial sequence learning) that rely on spatial working memory and attention (executive processes). It used voxelwise, group-level SPM analyses and reports peak coordinates and cluster results for contrasts (e.g., M_SEQ − M_PRED and M_ROT − M_PRED) against an active sensory control (S). Participant information (N=12; mean age 35.6, range 22–59) confirms a healthy adult sample. Imaging modality (H2 15O PET), detailed task paradigms, and whole-brain statistical maps are described. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, or out-of-range/clinical sample) apply. Thus the study meets all required inclusion criteria and is appropriate for a meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

Exclusion E8 applies: the sample includes participants outside the specified age range (reported age range 33–61 years; includes age 61 > 60). Study meets all inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing working memory), I6 (within-participant contrasts including task/stimulus-type contrasts), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrast maps reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/text), I9 (working memory is an executive function domain), and I10 (participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). No other exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Because E8 is violated, the study must be excluded despite satisfying inclusion criteria.

This is an event-related fMRI study of working memory/proactive interference (an executive function) in healthy adults (mean age 23.5). It reports within-participant contrasts (PI vs. nPI; retrieval-phase contrasts relative to a nonmnemonic active control), conducts group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses, and provides whole-brain voxel coordinates and activation maps. Imaging modality, participant health/age, and task paradigm are clearly reported. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met.

This fMRI study used an auditory one-back working memory task (executive function: working memory) with manipulated perceptual load (low vs high), providing within-subject contrasts (high vs low load and visibility interactions). Group-level random-effects analyses were conducted and voxelwise whole-brain exploratory analyses are reported (PFDR whole-brain checks), with coordinates reported for significant effects; results are presented as statistical maps/coordinates and figures. Participants were healthy adults (ages 21–31/22–30), imaging modality is fMRI, and the task paradigm is described in detail. All required reporting (methods, results, participant info) is present in the full text. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, includes active task conditions beyond rest, healthy adult sample). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

Exclusion E8 met: the study includes adolescent participants (mid-adolescence; Tanner stage reported) in addition to adults, so participants fall outside the target 18–60 healthy adult range and cannot be included in a meta-analysis restricted to healthy adults. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing cognitive control/emotional Stroop), I6 (within-subject contrasts: rejection>neutral and rejection>acceptance using active control conditions), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures), I9 (task taps an executive function domain—inhibition/cognitive control), I10 (reporting of participant ages, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm). Inclusion criteria not met: none. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded solely because of E8 (participants outside target adult age range).

Although this is an event-related fMRI study of executive function (attentional set shifting/cognitive flexibility) with within-subject task contrasts and reported group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses, the manuscript as provided does not report participant age information nor explicitly state confirmation that the sample were healthy adults. Inclusion criterion I10 requires reporting of participant age and confirmation of healthy sample status; this criterion is not met in the provided full text. Therefore not all inclusion criteria are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered based on the provided content.

Full text is incomplete (only title/metadata/redirect present). Based on available information: I5 (fMRI) is evident from title/journal metadata. There is insufficient information to confirm I6 (within-participant contrast vs active control), I7/I8 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I9 (task falls within established executive function domains), or I10 (reported participant ages and confirmation of healthy sample). No exclusion criteria can be confidently applied from the truncated content. Therefore I must exclude due to inability to verify required inclusion criteria from the incomplete full text.

Although this PET study clearly assesses executive function (working memory) with task-based within-subject contrasts and reports group-level, voxelwise SPM results, it includes clinical participants (hypertensive patients) and is not restricted to healthy adults. The inclusion of patient groups (and at least some participants reportedly above age 60) violates exclusion criterion E8 (studies not restricted to healthy individuals and/or outside the 18–60 age range). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: none of the I-criteria themselves fail, but exclusion E8 applies. Therefore the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis limited to healthy adults aged 18–60.

This is a task-based fMRI study of inhibitory control during episodic retrieval (retrieval-induced forgetting), addressing executive function (interference resolution/inhibition). It includes a within-subject contrast of selective retrieval (selection) versus nonselective re-exposure (active control), uses whole-brain, group-level voxelwise SPM analyses reported with peak coordinates and figures, and reports participant demographics (22 healthy adults, ages 20–29), imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and detailed task paradigm. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group only, empirical healthy adult sample).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 18–36) that includes a working memory (visual short-term memory, VSTM) task—a recognized executive function domain. Analyses include within-participant, parametric regressors (K-weighted and linear set-size) and group-level, whole-brain (random-effects) voxelwise statistical maps (FDR-corrected), with coordinates and figures reported. Participant health status, age range, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigms are provided. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that explicitly investigates working memory (an executive function) during a delayed-recognition kinesthetic task. The study reports within-participant parametric contrasts of task difficulty (set size 3>2>1>0) and delay-period memory-load effects, uses group-level whole-brain voxelwise random-effects SPM analyses with reported coordinates and cluster thresholds, and provides participant demographics (ages, health status), imaging modality, and task details. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group activations, uses active task baselines, empirical data, participants within 18–60). Full text is complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults investigating hypothesis generation/set-shift problems (executive/cognitive flexibility). It reports within-subject contrasts (Match Problems vs active baseline) and additional within-condition contrasts (successful vs unsuccessful; parametric modulation). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (SPM2) with corrected thresholds and MNI coordinates in tables/figures. Participant demographics and health status (healthy, mean age 26.3) and imaging modality (fMRI) and task paradigm are clearly described. Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study investigating conflict during bimanual reaching, specifically goal-selection and movement-related conflict (i.e., response-selection/cognitive control). It reports within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs congruent; symbolic vs spatial) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM, thresholding, cluster correction) with tables of coordinates. Participants are healthy adults (N=19 recruited; ages 18–31; right-handed), imaging modality is fMRI (1.5T), and the task paradigm and results are fully described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, uses active task contrasts, empirical study in healthy adults within age range). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, refs). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of executive function/task activations in healthy adults.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of response inhibition/selective movement prevention (an executive control domain). It reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., stop > go; stop selective > stop all), performed group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with cluster correction, and provides coordinates/figures and detailed methods. Participants are healthy adults (ages 22–40), modality is fMRI, and the paradigm is described. The full-text content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text is complete. This is an fMRI study in healthy adults with within-subject contrasts (self > other) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with coordinates and cluster tables; participant age, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigms are reported. However, the experimental tasks (conceptual self-reference and agentic self-reference/item selection) probe self-referential processing and mnemonic/agency effects rather than established executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation). Therefore key inclusion criteria are not met: I5 (study assessing executive function/cognitive control) and I9 (task falls within established executive function domains) are not satisfied. I6 (within-participant contrast of an executive function task vs active control) is also not applicable because the contrasts do not target executive function. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Conclusion: exclude because the study does not investigate executive function tasks as defined by the review objective; meets I7, I8, and I10 but fails I5, I6, and I9.

Excluded because the study uses block-design task vs rest baseline without an active control condition, meeting exclusion criterion E6. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI including cognitive tasks, including a four-choice reaction task interpreted as involving planning/cognitive load), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps and coordinate tables), I8 (results reported in figures/tables with coordinates), I9 (at least one task—4CRT—falls within an executive domain, e.g., planning/response selection), and I10 (healthy adult sample, ages reported, imaging modality and task paradigm described). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast of an executive function task relative to an active control condition; the contrasts are task versus rest). Full text appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDED due to E6.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults explicitly examining working memory (an established executive function domain) for face identity vs emotion. It reports within-participant contrasts between task conditions (identity vs emotion) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with thresholding and cluster results. Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality, and detailed task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, do not use rest/fixation as the only baseline, and participants are healthy adults within the 18–60 range. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) are satisfied and the study should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (an established executive function) in healthy adults (mean age 27.4) that reports group-level, whole-brain task analyses and coordinates. The experiment includes within-participant contrasts of experimental (working memory) tasks versus active control tasks, and task PLS produced whole-brain activation patterns (with local maxima/coordinates) suitable for meta-analysis. Connectivity analyses are also present but do not replace the whole-brain task activation results. All required participant, imaging modality, and task details are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-groups only, includes active control, empirical, and participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=38 females, age range 21.1–40.6). The task recruits executive processes (working memory, uncertainty management, cognitive control/conflict monitoring) and reports within-subject contrasts of task conditions (feedback types; learning phases) using group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM2 analyses. Results are reported as whole-brain voxelwise maps and coordinate tables; task paradigm and imaging modality are clearly described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, not resting-only baseline, not non-empirical, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Thus all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study tests memory-guided saccadic sequences with within-subject contrasts (New vs Rest, Familiar vs Rest, New vs Familiar) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM results with thresholding and coordinates/figures). The task explicitly engages spatial working memory, sequence planning and selection—domains of executive function. Participant details (ten healthy right-handed females, age 22–30), imaging modality (3T fMRI) and detailed task paradigm are reported. The resting control retained the same audio/visual stimulation while subjects maintained central fixation, serving as an appropriate active baseline controlling for sensory/auditory input; thus the within-participant contrasts are suitable for isolating executive components. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 and does not violate exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

The study reports fMRI group-level, whole-brain activation for a sustained attention/working memory task (PVSAT) in both MS patients and matched healthy controls, and provides participant demographics and task details. However, the task baseline/contrast used in the reported within-group analyses is rest/fixation (AB blocks of activation vs rest) rather than an active control condition. This violates inclusion criterion I6 and falls under exclusion criterion E6 (rest/fixation as the only baseline). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis despite meeting other inclusion criteria.

The study is an fMRI, whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analysis in healthy adult participants and reports coordinates. It includes a within-subject contrast (semantic categorization > passive listening). However, the task is a semantic language categorization task, not an established executive function domain (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria I5 (study assessing executive function/cognitive control) and I9 (task within established executive function domains), and consequently I6 (contrast of an executive function task vs active control) is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion).

This study uses task-based fMRI with a verbal fluency (silent word generation) vs active control (number listing) contrast and reports group-level whole-brain activations; however, the sample includes a postmenopausal/aged group with ages up to 68 years. The review exclusion criterion E8 disallows studies that include participants outside 18–60 years or are not restricted to healthy individuals. Because this study includes participants aged 60–68 (mean age 63 in the aged group) and is not restricted to the 18–60 range, it must be excluded despite meeting the analytic and reporting inclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI, task-based study comparing motor imagery (MI) and visual imagery (VI) in CFS patients and matched healthy controls. It reports within-subject contrasts (MI vs VI), whole-brain random-effects analyses with corrected clusters and stereotactic coordinates, and provides participant ages and other sample information. These features satisfy inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10. However, the study includes both patients (CFS) and healthy controls rather than being restricted to healthy individuals. This violates exclusion criterion E8 (not restricted to healthy individuals). Because any exclusion criterion met requires exclusion, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis despite meeting the other inclusion criteria.

This is a task-based PET study in healthy adults (ages reported 18–29 and 20–27) that investigates cognitive control/executive processes (recognition, response reversal, set-shifting, concurrent discrimination) and contrasts non-stereotyped versus stereotyped retrieval. It reports within-participant, group-level voxelwise analyses using SPM (voxelwise contrasts, cluster thresholds, corrected inference) and provides coordinates and figures. Active control conditions (visuomotor controls, fixation/passive viewing) and multiple within-subject contrasts are used. Participant health status, imaging modality (PET), and detailed task paradigms are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (this is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not resting-state-only, not non-empirical, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a structural MRI volumetric ROI study of prefrontal cortex degeneration in aging and Alzheimer disease. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain task-evoked results) and E8 (participants are outside 18–60 years and sample includes clinical AD patients, not restricted to healthy adults). No inclusion criteria are satisfied: it is not a task-based fMRI or PET study (I5 not met), contains no within-participant task vs active-control contrasts (I6 not met), provides no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps or coordinate activation tables for executive tasks (I7/I8 not met), does not report any executive function task activations (I9 not met), and although participant age and health information are reported, the imaging modality is structural MRI rather than fMRI/PET and no task paradigm is provided (I10 not met). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is incomplete (HTML header only). Cannot verify whether this is an fMRI/PET study of executive function or includes within-participant whole-brain contrasts. Based on available information, no inclusion criteria can be confirmed. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/uncertain: I5 (no evidence of task-based fMRI/PET assessing executive function), I6 (no within-participant contrast reported), I7/I8 (no whole-brain results or coordinate tables available), I9 (task domain not described as an executive function), I10 (participant age/health/imaging details not reported). No exclusion criteria from the list can be definitively applied with the available information (exclusion IDs met: none). Set fulltext_incomplete=true. Further assessment requires complete article content (methods/results).

Although this is an fMRI study of executive function using a within-subject active contrast (‘search’ vs ‘maintain’) and reports participant and task details, the group analyses are based on voxel counts in manually defined volumes-of-interest (VOIs) and GLM on these ROI counts rather than providing group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps or coordinate tables. Therefore it does not meet the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise group results (I7) and effectively reports ROI-only analyses, triggering exclusion criterion E3. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I9, I10. Inclusion criterion not met: I7. Exclusion criteria met: E3.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that directly probes short-term/working memory (an executive function domain) using a pitch memory task. The study reports within-participant contrasts (pitch memory > active motor control) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM99) with coordinates, thresholds, and cluster results. Participant age (18–40), healthy status, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group task activations, uses an active control). Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria listed below.

The study uses an affective face-processing fMRI task (matching fearful/angry faces) and investigates COMT genotype effects on limbic/prefrontal reactivity and connectivity. While it provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation maps and adequate participant/imaging details (satisfying I7, I8, I10), the paradigm is not an executive function or cognitive control task (does not fall into working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation). Therefore it fails I5 and I9, and does not meet I6 (within-participant contrast of an executive function task vs active control). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

Although this is an fMRI task of verbal short-term memory (working memory) with within-subject STM vs active REF contrasts and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported, the participant sample is not within the target age range for the meta-analysis (participants aged 62–85) and includes clinical Alzheimer's disease patients (not restricted to healthy adults). This violates exclusion criterion E8 (participants outside age range 18–60 and not restricted to healthy individuals). Therefore the study is excluded.

This study used PET but as resting (FDG) scanning with subjects resting; cognitive testing was behavioral and performed after PET. No task-based PET/fMRI activation contrasts or within-participant task vs active control contrasts are reported, and no whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps are provided. Participants include PTSD patients and healthy controls (not restricted to healthy adults). Therefore it fails inclusion criteria requiring task-based imaging, within-participant contrasts, and whole-brain activation maps and violates exclusions E5, E6, and E8.

Although this is an empirical, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults (reported ages and sample health) and provides voxelwise results/coordinates, the experimental paradigm does not target established executive-function domains for this meta-analysis. The task manipulates emotional prosody and selective auditory attention during a gender-decision task; primary contrasts are emotion (angry vs neutral) and attention (to-be-attended vs to-be-ignored). There is no within-participant contrast that isolates an executive function or cognitive-control task (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance) relative to an active control condition. Therefore I6 and I9 are not met, and the study does not address the meta-analysis objective despite meeting other reporting criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 18–26) that explicitly examines executive-function components (response selection and inhibitory control) using task-based paradigms. It includes within-participant contrasts (Incompatible vs Compatible response mapping) and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with peak activations and figures/tables of coordinates. Tasks fall within established executive function domains (response selection/inhibition). Participant characteristics, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigms are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group activations, uses active control conditions, empirical dataset, healthy adult sample within 18–60). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; therefore fulltext_incomplete is false.

Exclusion based on E8: study includes participants outside the 18–60 age range (control range 20–64 y; TBI range 21–65 y), violating the meta-analysis age restriction. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive processes via auditory oddball), I7 (group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/text), I9 (task probes executive domains: attention/working-memory updating), I10 (participant ages, healthy control status, imaging modality, and paradigm reported). Inclusion criterion I6 is not clearly met: while the study modeled targets, novels, and standards, the paper reports main effects (target and novel detection) relative to implicit baseline and does not explicitly present a within-participant contrast of the executive task relative to an active control condition (e.g., target > standard) in the healthy sample. Full text appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDE due to E8.

This is an fMRI, whole-brain, group-level study with healthy adult participants and clearly described tasks and methods. However, the experimental paradigms are language tasks (reading aloud and lexical decision) aimed at contrasting vowel vs. consonant processing, not established executive function tasks. Although the authors interpret a right middle frontal activation as related to inhibitory/no-go processing in the lexical decision condition, the study does not manipulate or target an executive function domain (e.g., dedicated inhibition, working memory, cognitive flexibility) as the primary task, nor does it present a within-participant contrast of an explicit executive-control task versus an active control designed to isolate executive processes. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I5, I6, and I9. No exclusion criteria are directly met. Full text appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is a task-based fMRI study of executive function (overt letter verbal fluency) in healthy adult volunteers; it reports within-participant contrasts of the executive task versus an active control condition (word repetition); group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) activation maps and cluster/coordinate results are reported and illustrated; reporting of whole-brain results appears in tables/figures and is described in the text; verbal fluency is an established executive domain (initiation/lexical retrieval); and participant demographics, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are clearly provided. None of the exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-group task activations, uses an active control, is empirical human neuroimaging, participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete.

The study is excluded because it includes older adults (beyond the 18–60 range), violating E8. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of an executive process), I6 (within-participant contrasts: refresh vs read), I7 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked results reported as regional activations), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures), I9 (task maps onto executive function—selection/refreshing), I10 (reports participant age groups, healthy samples, imaging modality, and task paradigm). Inclusion criteria not met: none. Note: the provided full text appears to be abstract-level and is likely incomplete (core methods/results/discussion not fully present), so fulltext_incomplete=true.

This study is not a task-based fMRI or PET investigation of executive function. Inclusion IDs met: none.
